title: perf(server): very long threads open about 10x faster
author: t3dotgg
head: 5c870548c45f506093b9210cae53c99b68d93593
body:
Opening a very long thread was slow. One real thread (230 turns, 41,000 items, still running) showed "Loading messages..." for a long time. The server read for its first page walked thousands of tool-call rows and sent 3.15 MB for 77 visible rows.

Two causes:

1. **The window search walked every tool call.** To find the newest conversation rows, the read scanned all rows since the last boundary. Migration 082 adds a partial index over conversation rows, and the search reads from it. A running turn is read from the run index.
2. **Old todo lists pulled the whole history into every window.** A todo list is never closed when its run ends. Each one counted as live work, so every window carried the nodes, subagents, provider turns, plans and checkpoints of old runs. A todo list of a run that is no longer live does not count now.

The window also keeps the newest ready checkpoint always, so the diff of the last finished turn stays available during a long run.

## Result

Measured on a copy of a real 3.7 GB database, old code against this branch, for that thread:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First read | 2,230 ms | 31 ms |
| Warm read | 244 ms | 19 ms |
| Wire snapshot | 3.15 MB | 0.39 MB |
| Subagents in the window | 413 | 28 |

## Proof

- Old and new `getThreadSnapshotWindow` return the same timeline rows for all 625 threads in that database (1,875 reads: cold, cold without deferral, one older page; 0 mismatches).
- New assertions in `ProjectionStore.test.ts` fail on `m [...]

title: test(web): theme search test no longer flakes on slow runners
author: t3dotgg
head: 58d65b0f1f077a31846a095b90dce4377c6369a0
body:
## Problem

`ThemeImportDialog.browser.test.tsx > searches Open VSX under StrictMode` fails on CI with:

```
expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ 'night', ObjectContaining{…} ]
1st vi.fn() call: [ "n", { signal, sortBy: "downloadCount" } ]
```

In the last 24 hours it failed 17 CI runs on unrelated branches (12 of them passed on rerun) and 1 run on main.

The test typed `night` one key at a time. The search has a 350 ms debounce. On a slow runner one gap between keys is longer than that, so a search for the prefix `n` runs first. The mock returns "Nightfall" for every query, so the heading shows, and the test checks the mock before the debounce for `night` fires.

## Change

Test only. `userEvent.fill` replaces `userEvent.type`, so the input gets one input event. No prefix search can run, and the heading can show only after the `night` search. The StrictMode check stays the same: `fill` goes through the same `onChange` and debounce.

## Scope and approval

Focused fix for a flaky test that blocks unrelated PRs. No product code changes.

## Verification

- Old test with a forced 500 ms gap between `n` and `ight`: fails 3/3 with the exact CI message.
- With the fix: the full file passes 3/3.
- `vp run check:changed` passes.
- Not checked: a slow CI runner. PR CI runs the test once.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 pass with GPT-6.1 Sol. Sol verdict: approved

title: fix(web): long merged spreadsheet selections no longer crash
author: voltcrash
head: cff348c47a6929d8f047a2bd19af91b9937e03ab
body:
Selecting A15001:B15001 in a workbook with 15,000 valid, non-overlapping alternating-column merges overflows the spreadsheet preview's stack. Selection painting and copy synchronously rescan the entire merge list for every expansion.

Keep the usual one- or two-scan path, then use four sorted boundary sweeps for longer chains. Each overlap condition becomes true once as the selection grows, preserving transitive expansion with O(n log n) worst-case work and no recursive calls. The change is limited to the helper and its regression tests.

This qualifies for CONTRIBUTING.md's focused obvious-bug exception: it fixes a reproducible crash in an existing selection workflow without changing product behavior. Fresh searches found no matching open PR; #32693 and #31868 concern other document behavior.

Proof:
- The focused regression throws `RangeError` on base and passes after the fix; all 3 cases pass, covering both chain orders, all expansion edges, and unrelated merges.
- `vp run scenarios:prove` reports `failsOnBase: true`, `passesOnHead: true`. An isolated preview harness mounts the unmodified `OfficeFilePreview` and real archive/XLSX workers, loads all 15,000 merges, and drives selection and copy. Base returns no clipboard data; the fix paints the expanded range and copies 15,001 rows with both markers. The Browser panel independently reproduced the base stack overflow and verified the fix. title: fix(server): Copilot threads load optional T3 tools on demand
author: juliusmarminge
head: 383a0940524de88197194cdd76db0f6cce2f8931
body:
Cause: the T3 MCP server returns all 68 tools in tools/list to every client. Claude has its own ToolSearch and Pi defers tools in its extension (#17220), but Copilot over ACP has neither, so every request carried every schema (~25k tokens).

Fix: the ACP adapter flavor gets a `deferMcpTools` option (on for Copilot only). With it set, the HTTP MCP server entry Copilot receives also carries the header `t3-tool-exposure: deferred` (constant `MCP_TOOL_EXPOSURE_HEADER` in provider-core/mcpSession). On the server, a global `McpServer.visibility` gate in McpHttpServer.ts acts only on tools/list. For a thread caller sending that header it lists orchestrator_capabilities, delegate_task, task_status (the same direct set as Pi) plus a new `tool_search`, and anything that session has already loaded. Every other client gets its previous list minus `tool_search`. Calls are never gated. `tool_search` (toolkits/toolSearch, registered through toolkitRegistration/McpToolAccess.readsAsCaller) scores tools by name and description, loads up to 10 matches for the caller's providerSessionId (McpToolExposure, a map capped at the 256 newest sessions), and sends notifications/tools/list_changed. `layerToolSearch` sits outside `layerTools`, so the committed agent-context budget (what Claude and Codex see) is unchanged.

Copilot CLI 1.0.109 checked with a mock MCP server over ACP: it sends the custom header on every request. On list_changed (on the GET stream or inside the POST SSE response) it re-lists [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Exclude tools disabled for the searching caller.**

`server.tools` includes registered tools before their `EnabledWhen` checks run. When linked environments are off, `tool_search` can return `t3_environment_link` and record it as loaded, although the caller cannot list or call it. A subagent can get the same misleading result for `watch_pull_request`. Apply the caller's enabled-tool checks before returning search results. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/383a0940524de88197194cdd76db0f6cce2f8931/apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/orchestrator/tools.ts))

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Keep required PR-link actions discoverable at the required time.**

On a fresh deferred Copilot session, `link_pull_request` and `link_pull_requests` are absent from the advertised tools. `buildRuntimeInstructions` tells the agent to link each new PR as its next call. The agent must instead search first or attempt an unadvertised call. Keep the required tools direct, or change the deferred-client instructions to require search before linking. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/383a0940524de88197194cdd76db0f6cce2f8931/packages/provider-core/src/server/runtimeInstructions.ts))

** Minor** · **Performance & Scalability** · **Quick win**

**Notify clients only when a search loads a new tool.**

If a session repeats a successful query, `load` adds names already in its set, but this condition still broadcasts `list_changed`. Connected clients can then re-list unchanged tools. Make `load` report whether it added a name, and announce only when it did. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Effect-TS/effect/effect@4.1.2/packages/effect/src/ai/McpServer.ts))

title: fix(server): t3 serve no longer offers --auto-bootstrap-project-from-cwd
author: juliusmarminge
head: 9196b6b9963c4fd1415f48e18626fa8c87735f9e
body:
`serveCommand` was built from the full `sharedServerCommandFlags`, so `t3 serve --help` listed `--auto-bootstrap-project-from-cwd`. Serve always runs with `startupPresentation: "headless"` and `forceAutoBootstrapProjectFromCwd: false`, which `resolveServerConfig` checks before the flag, so the flag was accepted and silently ignored. The fix builds serve's flag set from the shared flags minus `autoBootstrapProjectFromCwd`, and the handler passes `autoBootstrapProjectFromCwd: Option.none()` to keep the `CliServerFlags` shape. Result: serve help no longer lists the flag, and passing it fails loudly with `Unrecognized flag: --auto-bootstrap-project-from-cwd in command t3 serve` (checked with the real CLI). Plain `t3` and the unlisted `start` keep the flag. Nothing in the repo passes it to serve; the dev runner uses the env var. No new regex or parser.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#34223

On origin/main 950c34226c (worktree, `vp i`): `node apps/server/src/bin.ts serve --help` lists `--auto-bootstrap-project-from-cwd  Create a project for the current working directory on startup when missing.` In a scratch git repo with one commit, ran `T3CODE_DEV_SEED=0 node apps/server/src/bin.ts serve --auto-bootstrap-project-from-cwd --base-dir  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 39231 --log-level debug .`: the debug line 'startup phase: publishing welcome event' showed bootstrapProjectId: undefined and bootstrapThreadId: undefined, no warning about the flag was logged, and after stoppi [...]

title: fix(git): stop new threads inheriting historical branch PRs
author: juliusmarminge
head: 997784dd6aac55a065765de95b1364ed94c31eca
body:
Fixes #31896: new threads on a long-lived branch no longer pick up a branch PR that was merged or closed before the thread was created, and the web/desktop Git-status fallback only shows open PRs. A PR checkout marks the branch in git config (`branch..t3-pull-request`) so threads created by checking out a finished PR keep it. Review item addressed and confirmed: the filter also cleared PRs a thread had already saved, so threads created by an explicit checkout before the upgrade (no marker) lost their PR, and the saved-reference fallback rejected it through the original completion-time check. Fix: ThreadPullRequestService only refuses a new association. A thread whose saved branchPullRequest is the detected PR keeps it, and the completion-time check on the saved-reference fallback is removed, so that path behaves as on main. The marker is still read only when some thread in the group would otherwise drop the PR. Trade-off: threads that wrongly saved a historical PR before the upgrade keep it (same as main); only new threads are protected. AI-assisted; verified with the tests and tools listed above.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#31896

Supersedes #31958. The change is @sldone's; their commits are kept.

## Reproduction on main

In a GitHub project whose default branch is main, create a long-lived staging branch, open a staging-to-main PR, and merge it without deleting staging. After the merge, create a new unrelated T3 Code thread using staging, complete a turn, and inspect the threa [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Resolve the marked PR before comparing its URL with the discovered PR.**

If a branch has several completed PRs, checking out an older PR does not make that PR the discovery result. `findLatestPrForHeadContext`, Lines 1943-1949, still selects the most recently updated match.

For example, checkout can store PR `#42` here while discovery returns a newer completed PR `#43`. This comparison returns `false`. The new thread then receives neither reference, although the user explicitly checked out `#42`.

Use the checkout reference as the discovery candidate for the checkout-created thread. Extend the existing checkout coverage with two completed PRs on the same branch.

** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Heavy lift**

**Scope the checkout exception to the checkout-created thread.**

After a user checks out a completed PR on `staging`, this marker also exempts every later thread on `staging` from the historical-PR filter. `ThreadPullRequestService.ts`, Line 237, checks only the branch and URL. It cannot distinguish the checkout-created thread from unrelated threads created later.

Persist the explicit association on the checkout-created thread, or give the exception a thread identity. Otherwise, checking out one historical PR restores the inheritance problem for that branch while the marker remains.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Include Bitbucket completion times in branch discovery**

Bitbucket branch listings omit both terminal timestamps. On a reused non-default branch, the guard therefore accepts an old merged or closed PR for a new thread. The thread can show that historical PR in its sidebar.

Request and propagate the completion timestamp before applying this guard. Preserve associations for threads created before completion and for explicitly checked-out PRs.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Preserve PRs discovered after a thread is settled.**

If a PR opens after its thread settles, periodic discovery skips that thread. When Git status later reports the PR as merged, the badge and link can disappear because no association was saved. Ensure discovery can save PRs opened during the thread’s lifetime without restoring PRs that closed before the thread was created.

title: fix(server): one dropped probe no longer lists a live linked peer as unreachable
author: juliusmarminge
head: 7e69f920f250363c323b9b6668d3312ec6721ad7
body:
Both review items were correct and describe one defect: the single retry in PeerLinks `describe` fired immediately, so it failed inside the same 0.1-0.4 s network drop. The retry now waits 1 second (`Schedule.spaced("1 second")`). It keeps the certificate exclusion and stays inside the existing probe timeout (3 s loopback / 10 s otherwise). A fast failure such as a reset or 503 is retried after the network has had time to recover. A peer that is really down still reports within the same timeout as before. The repro test now uses it.live instead of it.effect, because the retry's 1 s wait never elapses on TestClock; it is a real local HTTP network fixture, which AGENTS.md allows for it.live, and its assertion is unchanged. In a temporary, uncommitted change to the test, a peer answering 503 to every request for a 400 ms window listed as reachable.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#34195

## Reproduction on main

Commit a03d9bce02 (origin/main). Ran two local servers: A via `T3CODE_DEV_SEED=0 vp run dev --home-dir /homeA` (server+web) and B via `node apps/server/src/bin.ts serve --base-dir /homeB --port 47101`, both with linkedEnvironmentsEnabled=true. Put a TCP proxy on 127.0.0.1:47102 -> B that resets only the next connection when armed. Linked A to B with `t3 environment link http://127.0.0.1:47102 --pairing-code  --access full-access`. `t3 environment list` on A: reachable. Armed one reset: unreachable. Next list: reachable again (proxy log PASS, DROP, PASS). In the web client on A, a [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Performance & Scalability** · **Quick win**

**Skip retries for permanent HTTP responses.**

If a descriptor URL returns 404, this predicate retries it after one second. Effect 4.1.2 exposes that response status on the client error. Each stale URL can therefore add a second to `list` or `resolve` before the next URL is checked. Retry transient responses and transport failures, but return immediately for permanent 4xx responses. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Effect-TS/effect/effect@4.1.2/packages/effect/src/http-api/HttpApiClient.ts))

title: fix(server): preview automation reports ambiguous selectors instead of calling them invalid
author: juliusmarminge
head: 91496754d623805a53826cf062ea75cc72811263
body:
toOperationError in apps/server/src/preview/ServerBrowserPage.ts sorted Playwright's 'strict mode violation' (a valid selector that matched several elements) together with real parse errors and tagged it PreviewAutomationInvalidSelectorError. The broker then replaced Playwright's text with the generic 'received an invalid selector ... selector takes CSS' guidance, which hid that the selector was ambiguous. Removing 'strict mode violation' from that regex sends these errors down the existing PreviewAutomationExecutionError path, which keeps Playwright's first line ('... strict mode violation: locator(...) resolved to 2 elements'), so the agent can narrow the selector. Real parse errors ('while parsing selector', 'Unknown engine', 'Unexpected token') are still reported as invalid selectors. No new regex was added; one alternative was removed from an existing anchor-free alternation, which stays linear-time. The repro test from factory/repro-34198 is kept unchanged. The only other edit is in the shared test fixture: its throwing locator mock was declared as returning unknown, so the repro test's mockImplementation typechecks (the inferred return type had been never). This was proven with the unit test, not re-checked in a live preview browser.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#34198

## Reproduction on main

Commit a03d9bce02 (origin/main). Started `T3CODE_DEV_SEED=0 vp run dev` in a fresh worktree, paired the preview browser to the dev web app, opened the new-thread composer at 2200x1000 [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Keep parse-error phrases in selector values out of the invalid-selector classification.**

If two buttons have `aria-label='Unexpected token'`, Playwright’s strict-mode message can include that valid selector. The regex then matches the quoted value and returns `PreviewAutomationInvalidSelectorError`, although the selector is ambiguous, not invalid. Identify a strict-mode failure before searching its message for parse-error phrases, or limit the parse-error match to observed parser-error prefixes.

title: fix(server): a busy embedded frame no longer holds copy keys back
author: juliusmarminge
head: f5f438fb175a6f2dc4d07b5ea15e5eceff921fdd
body: Item 1 holds and is fixed. At 8ce3250, takeCopy(since) removed the oldest entry at or after since in every frame, and the server kept the first non-empty result. A read delayed by a busy frame therefore also consumed a later shortcut's entry in another frame and dropped it. Now each copy/cut key has a closed millisecond window. since is Date.now() just before Input.dispatchKeyEvent, and until is Date.now() after it resolves; the keydown and the copy/cut event run before that acknowledgement. ServerTab.copyKeyedUntil records the last until, and the next copy key waits (at most 1 ms, via the existing sleepUntil) until Date.now() > copyKeyedUntil, so windows never share a millisecond. takeCopy(since, until) drops entries older than since (stale) and takes the oldest remaining entry only if its time is <= until, so an entry can match only the key that made it, whatever frame it is in. Reads still run one at a time per tab in key order, outside the input queue, so later keys and clicks are not held by a busy frame and the earlier double-cut fix stays. Checked in real Chromium (playwright-core, two recorder pages standing in for main page and responsive frame): cut 'main first', cut 'main second', cut 'frame third'; the reads for windows 1-3 returned ["main first","main second","frame third"]. The cross-frame case is not in the unit tests: the matching is in the injected browser script, which the mocked CDP tests cannot run. The full scenarios:prove run was not re-run. No new regex [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Maintainability & Code Quality** · **Heavy lift**

**Test stale copies in the real recorder.**

Add a focused test where another frame retains a copy with a timestamp before the current key. Assert that it is not sent to the viewer, and that a current copy is returned. The existing tests mock the recorder, so they cannot catch removal of the `since` filter.

✅ Addressed in commit f5f438f

** Minor** · **Performance & Scalability** · **Quick win**

**Bound the pending clipboard entries.**

When an embedded-frame read stalls, later copy keys still reach the responsive main frame. Each key adds an entry containing up to `CLIPBOARD_TEXT_LIMIT` characters. However, `tab.copyReads` prevents subsequent reads from draining those entries until the stalled read finishes.

Repeated copy keys can therefore retain an unbounded amount of clipboard text. Bound the queue and define its overflow behavior.

** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Heavy lift**

**Preserve copies until their reads complete.**

This wait does not wait for `tab.copyReads`. If a frame stalls the first read, a second cut can reach the page while its read waits. A subsequent navigation can destroy the document and its recorder before that read starts. The cut text is then lost after being removed from the page.

Preserve unread entries across navigation, or prevent navigation from discarding them. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/f5f438fb175a6f2dc4d07b5ea15e5eceff921fdd/apps/server/src/preview/ServerBrowserStream.ts))

** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Heavy lift**

**Do not wait for an adjustable wall clock to catch up.**

If the system clock moves backward after a copy, the next copy waits until `Date.now()` passes the old timestamp. This wait holds the control queue, so later input and control handoffs can stall for the size of the clock adjustment. Use a monotonic ordering mechanism that remains comparable across the recorder and server. ([developer.mozilla.org](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Performance_API/High_precision_timing?utm_source=openai))

title: fix(desktop): an SSH password prompt that ended leaves the dialog instead of stacking
author: Umais-Adeed
head: d63e039c6d57665664c0bdeae84cd9c34e0866f2
body:
## Problem

After sleep, a locked screen, or any background reconnect nobody answers, the desktop app shows an expired **SSH verification required** prompt. Dismiss reveals another expired one, sometimes many in a row, and the only way out is restarting the app (#7699, with reports from macOS on 0.0.34 through 0.1.6).

The window is never told when a password request ends:
- `DesktopSshPasswordPrompts` removes a request from its pending map when it is answered, cancelled, times out or is interrupted, but it only ever sends the window new requests (`desktop:ssh-password-prompt`).
- `SshPasswordPromptDialog` appends every request to its queue, and `removeSshPasswordPrompt` only drops the head.

Each background reconnect that asks for a password adds another entry. When those requests time out in the main process, they stay queued in the window, expired.

## Change

- `DesktopSshPasswordPrompts` sends `desktop:ssh-password-prompt-settled` with the request id from the cleanup every request already runs, so it covers every way a prompt ends. The preload exposes it as `onSshPasswordPromptSettled`, and `DesktopBridge` declares it.
- The dialog's queue removes a settled prompt wherever it sits, not only at the head. It also ignores a request id it already holds. The prompt on screen is therefore always one the main process is still waiting on. Dismiss stays as it is.

This is desktop-only: SSH environments exist only in the desktop app.

Fixes #7699, which has  [...]

title: fix(web): hide empty replies when renders show the result
author: Yash-Singh1
head: 1335e1439563efcef4e66380cc3016142837c510

author: Umais-Adeed
head: 9c174f7f355af036631a089e30946acf37827814
body:
## Problem

In a pull request's Code tab, marking a file **Viewed** folds it. If you close the right panel (or open another right-panel tab) and come back, or change the commit scope, every file is expanded again while its Viewed tick stays. Reviewers working through several PRs lose their place, as okaisti describes in #13279. screen-gd, Mnigos and moinmir reproduced it on nightlies up to `0.1.4-nightly.20261028.3824`, and Mnigos recorded the remount path.

`PullRequestCodeTab` keeps fold state only as `toggledFiles` and `foldOverride` in local state. A remount starts both empty, and a scope change clears them. `isFileDiffCollapsed` decides folding from those two alone, so the persisted Viewed marks never feed into it.

- `isFileDiffCollapsed` takes whether the file is viewed. A viewed, non-stale file is folded by default. A stale mark means the file changed after it was viewed, so it opens like any other file.

title: fix(server): auto thread sends queue while a turn is stopping
author: tanav29
head: 35e4aa4d0aa7c21467b52bc06ce269eaeeae54c3
body:
## Problem

An MCP `t3_thread_send` with `mode: "auto"` fails if Stop has reached the target run but its provider turn still reports running. The service resolves the send to a steer and drops its automatic delivery intent, so the orchestrator treats it as an explicit steer and stores a rejected command receipt.

## Change

Preserve `deliveryIntent: "auto"` when dispatching an automatic send. The orchestrator can then use its existing Stop guard to queue the message. Explicit steering still fails, and an agent's message preserves the user's queue hold.

The regression uses a running provider session with steering capabilities and checks automatic queueing, explicit-steer rejection, and idempotent retry.

## Scope and approval

Fixes #34158.

This qualifies as a very small, focused fix for an obvious bug: one service-boundary field makes the reported automatic send follow the orchestrator's existing delivery policy. It adds no new workflow, setting, or provider behavior.

## Problem

OpenCode shell tools can return when a background command launches. T3 now keeps that command in its existing background activity UI until it exits or is stopped, retains captured output, and preserves native completion notifications and continuation turns.

## Change

The adapter scopes tracking and Stop to the owning session and its descendants. Recovery uses the experimental shell-job inventory on OpenCode 2.2.6+, with shell-list fallback on supported older servers. After a cold resume, recovered output, terminal state, and idle roster snapshots persist through the existing session event pump before another turn starts. New session-scoped activity is restricted to attached threads and uses the persisted run identity when available so it stays in the current timeline. Polling reads run outside the adapter lock, with stale results discarded after Stop, exit, or another read. Recovery and Stop retain bounded I/O. Final reads retain the output tail, including diagnostics beyond the first four pages. The SDK remains pinned to 2.0.28, and main's native goals, todo checklists, and image jobs are preserved.

## Scope and approval

Maintainer-directed implementation of native OpenCode background shell tracking from the T3 Code handoff. title: fix(server): Find frees searched thread text after one idle minute
author: t3dotgg
head: 037889c9c1dda0b64d71457aa75eaaace95251ac
body:
Find keeps the parsed text of the threads you searched in memory until the server restarts. The caches have a one-minute TTL, but Effect's `Cache` only expires an entry when that same key is read again, so nothing is freed after you close Find. The results of the last 8 completed queries are also kept with no expiry.

Now the two parsed-text caches and the completed-query map are one resource held in an `RcRef` with a one-minute idle time. Each search borrows it for its whole stream, and all of it is dropped one minute after the last search ends. Text entries are keyed by message content, so they never go stale, and the per-entry TTL is gone. On `main` that TTL counts from the first parse, so a Find session longer than 60 seconds parses the thread again while you type.

This is a smaller answer to the concern in [#32613](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/32613). It keeps the library cache and the entry limits from [#20801](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/20801). Memory while Find is in use has the same entry limits as `main`. This PR does not lower that peak. It only frees the memory when Find is idle.

One behavior change: a repeated query after one idle minute scans the thread again. On `main` it used the stored result.

## Proof

One new test in `ThreadFind.test.ts` with exact parse counts. It fails on `main` and passes here. It covers:
- a search that is in progress across one idle minute holds the caches,
- searches less than one minute apart parse each m [...]

title: fix(scripts): scenarios run where localhost resolves to IPv6 first
author: juliusmarminge
head: 5379f98d7a0860a711917b363c2316599968db42
body:
## Problem

`vp run scenarios` and `vp run scenarios:prove` (added in pingdotgg/t3code#34007) could not run on machines that resolve `localhost` to `::1` first, such as the Linux worker VMs. e2e waited on `http://127.0.0.1:` for its full 300-second startup timeout on each commit and then reported "could not run", although the app had started.

Confirmed on a fresh worker VM at `3a8c250cb0`: the web dev server binds `localhost`, which there is `[::1]` only.

$ getent hosts localhost
::1             localhost ip6-localhost ip6-loopback
➜  Local:   http://localhost:35054/        # ss: [::1]:35054
127.0.0.1 -> no answer        [::1] -> 200

Setting `HOST` from outside cannot fix it: the dev runner deletes `HOST` in web modes.

The runner and the app now agree on one address by construction.

- `scripts/e2e.config.ts` has one `LOOPBACK` constant (`127.0.0.1`) used for the app URL, the ready URL, and passed to the start script.

title: feat(server): voice models reuse copies already on disk
author: juliusmarminge
head: f2e0793b0ebbd1f99827b8d8eee4950585e2f94c
body:
## Problem

Every app that ships local speech-to-text downloads its own copy of the same models. T3 Code always fetched from Hugging Face into its own folder, even when the identical file was already on the machine.

## Fix

- **Download looks first.** Before fetching, the model store checks Handy's `models` folder and the Hugging Face cache for the pinned file and links it instead of downloading.
- **Use existing.** Settings → Voice has a path field under the model list. Paste a model file or a folder; the server searches it (five levels deep) and links every catalog model it finds.
- **Only catalog files.** A candidate must match a catalog model's size and SHA-256, so the store still never loads a file the catalog does not pin. Other formats (Core ML, ONNX, MLX) are not usable.
- **No copy.** A match is installed as a symlink, with a hard-link fallback where symlinks are not allowed.
- **Way out.** A linked model shows the file it uses, and its delete button becomes unlink. Removing it deletes only the link.

Older servers do not report `supportsModelLinking`, so the path field is hidden for them. Mobile has no path field; linked models appear there as installed and can be selected.

## Evidence

Before: the model list with the new path field.

![Before](https://git.cafe/api/attachments/attach_01m73tpjwzect8npkz9pr7hcch)

After linking a folder that holds Moonshine Tiny:

![After](https://git.cafe/api/attachments/attach_01m73tpkr6eh2bynzkycx9myx5)

Live run on a dev server: [...]

**Link replacement is not atomic. A failure leaves the model uninstalled.**

Line 258 removes `finalPath` before the link exists. If `fs.symlink` and the `fs.link` fallback both fail, the previously installed file is gone. The error propagates to the caller. In `download`, `Effect.orElseSucceed(() => [])` hides the failure, and the code then starts a network download.

## Problem

OpenCode's native image generation tool returns when it launches a job, so T3 could treat the tool call as finished before the image job completed. Users could also lose the final outcome and preview after a reconnect, especially when using a remote OpenCode server.

## Change

Track native image jobs as pending background tasks until OpenCode reports completion, failure, or cancellation. Retain the result in the original tool item, load completed image files for previews, and recover outcomes from message history or the image job list on supported OpenCode versions. Scope job reads to the owning session and support remote file reads.

## Scope and approval

This is a focused fix for the native OpenCode image job lifecycle. OpenCode's tool launch metadata and later outcome notices already identify the job, and its API exposes image job history in newer versions. The change uses those existing capabilities and keeps history recovery for older versions.

## Verification

Added focused protocol fixture coverage for completed, failed, and cancelled outcomes, session isolation, reconnect recovery through message history and the 2.2.6 job list, and remote image reads. Captured collapsed and expanded tool item screenshots in the T3 client using an image job fixture; no paid image generation was used.

body:
## Problem

In the open thread a screen reader hears a turn's status and nothing else: "Working", "Needs approval", "Needs your input", "Done". A long turn is silent between "Working" and "Done", so a blind user can't tell what the agent wrote or what it is doing without leaving the composer to read the timeline. Reported with NVDA in https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/26956.

## Change

**Screen reader announcements** in Settings → Chat sets how much of a turn is read, per device:

| Level | What is read |
|---|---|
| Status only (default) | What the app reads today. Nothing changes. |
| Status and messages | Also each message the agent finishes and then keeps working after, as "T3 Code: …". |
| Everything | Also the step the agent is on, such as "Running git", "Editing src/a.ts" or "Thinking". |

- The reply that closes the turn is not read. "Done" is, and the reply is in the timeline.

## Problem

Sending a new thread made the sidebar jump before the thread settled, on mobile and on web. There were two causes:

1. Mobile sends every new thread through the outbox, even on a live connection. While the create request was in flight, the thread showed under "Unsent" as a taller "Sends on reconnect" row.
2. The server commits a new thread (`thread.create`) before its first run (`message.dispatch`). That gap was about 150ms in the mobile recording and 15–40ms on a fast local machine. Offline, blocked or retrying sends stay listed under "Unsent" with their open and delete actions.

title: fix(server): preview snapshots keep page text beside large accessibility trees

head: 9d4c402fc822aa8a20be6a557e403e56331e3f81
body:
## Problem

`preview_snapshot` on a text page with a large accessibility tree returns `"visibleText": "…"`. The shrink loop that keeps the snapshot's metadata text under its 20,000-byte target starts the tree at up to 20,000 characters, and it halved the page text all the way to zero before it shrank the tree at all. A page whose tree alone fills that target hits it. Opening a synthetic 2,000-row table with `preview_open`, then calling `preview_snapshot`, returned `visibleText after 0 characters` in `omitted`.

Then page text shrinks to the floor, then the tree shrinks to the floor. Only after both are at the floor does the previous order resume (page text, then interactive elements, then the tree), so the loop aims at the same 20,000-byte target as before and ends with the same last steps. The tree's starting size, the byte target, and the `omitted` messages are unchanged.

title: fix(desktop): clear stale GPU caches when the Electron version changes
author: juliusmarminge
head: 44a2a6b3072d4741adb0a71c25e4500074a0a26a
body:
## Problem

After the Windows desktop app auto-updated to a nightly on Electron 44.10.1, scroll areas and icons painted blank on every launch (the previous nightly's Electron version is not known). Restarting did not fix it; clearing six Chromium GPU cache folders in `%APPDATA%\t3code-v2` did. Nothing in the desktop app invalidates those caches when the Electron build changes, so caches written by the previous build are reused after every update. Launching the built app on `main` with caches and a marker seeded as if written by Electron 44.10.0 shows the old cache contents surviving launches on 44.10.1.

## Change

- `clearStaleGpuCaches` (`DesktopUserData.ts`) compares a `gpu-cache-electron-version` marker in userData with the running Electron version.
- **Version differs or no marker:** it removes `GPUCache`, `GrShaderCache`, `ShaderCache`, `DawnGraphiteCache`, `DawnWebGPUCache` and `GPUPersistentCache`, then writes the marker. A relaunch on the same version keeps the warm caches.
- **Why the Electron version:** Electron patch releases carry Chromium backports under the same Chrome version, so a Chrome-version key would miss updates like this one.
- **When it runs:** synchronously in `DesktopClerk.make`, right after the single-instance lock, so a second launch never deletes caches the running instance has open.
  - Chromium opens these caches on the first event-loop turn, before `ready`, so this has to happen in that existing non-yielding pre-ready step.
  - The pre-ready f [...]

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Handle an undefined `electronVersion` at runtime.**

In Node-run `DesktopClerk` tests, `process.versions.electron` is undefined. If a marker exists under `/tmp/app-data/t3code-v2`, the test can delete its GPU caches before the write fails and logs a warning.

title: feat(server): watched GitHub pull requests react to host events, not only the 2-minute sweep
author: juliusmarminge
head: bd62ae1db07e6345c76f99359507ae4bedad4e5e
body:
Watched pull requests only noticed a push, review, merge or conflict at the next 2-minute sweep.

GitHub's new event subscriptions API (`/event-subscriptions`, currently a preview) streams pull request changes over SSE. The watch reactor now opens one subscription per watched github.com pull request and re-reads the pull request as soon as an event arrives, instead of waiting for the sweep. The sweep stays: checks have no events yet, and it is the fallback wherever a subscription is refused.

- `GitHubPullRequestEvents` subscribes, follows the stream, reconnects with jittered backoff, treats 45s of silence as a dead connection, renews expired subscriptions, and deletes the subscription when the watch ends. It emits once per connection so the reader catches up on anything missed while disconnected.
- If the app sign-in can't open a stream (the app isn't installed on that repository), it retries with the user's own credential.
- Other hosts and refused subscriptions keep today's polling.

Only users signed in through the GitHub app, which is still opt-in behind its flag, subscribe. Everyone else keeps polling and never calls the preview API.

Tested: the stream module against scripted responses (refused app token, reconnect, renewal, cleanup), the gate for users without the app sign-in, the reactor reading on an event without the clock moving, and a live run against github.com (subscribe, stream held past the silence limit on keep-alives, subscription deleted on stop).

title: fix(shared): Open in Zed ignores the OpenZFS zed daemon on Linux
author: juliusmarminge
head: 249557a16b82a56182a92e6a31968c49111af981
body:
## Problem

On Linux, editor discovery accepts any executable named `zed`. When the only one on PATH is the OpenZFS Event Daemon (no Zed editor installed), T3 lists Zed as available, shows "Open in Zed" as the default editor, and clicking it runs the ZFS daemon. Reproduced on main with the genuine `zed` from Ubuntu's zfs-zed 2.2.2 package as the only `zed` on the dev server's PATH: the thread header showed "Open in Zed", and clicking it ran the daemon, which printed "Must be run as root".

## Change

In `resolveEditorCommand` (`packages/shared/src/editor.ts`), on Linux a candidate named `zed` counts as the Zed editor only if ` --version` exits 0 and its output starts with `Zed` (the Zed CLI prints `Zed 1.27.0 … – …`). The OpenZFS daemon only takes short options, so `--version` makes it print usage and exit 1 without starting. The probe reads only the first chunk of output, has a 2 s timeout, and treats any failure (timeout, spawn error, crash) as "not Zed". A rejected path is skipped and discovery moves on to later candidates. `zeditor` still comes first and is never probed, and macOS and Windows are unchanged. The resolver now needs a `ChildProcessSpawner`. The server and desktop production layers already provide one, so only the desktop test layer needed a mock.

`resolveEditorLaunch` (`apps/server/src/process/externalLauncher.ts`) no longer falls back to the bare command when the resolver finds nothing. It fails with the existing "Editor command not found" error. For every [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Reject an unresolved Linux Zed launch.**

If `resolveEditorCommand` rejects all Linux Zed candidates, `resolveEditorLaunch` falls back to bare `zed`. A direct RPC request can then launch the OpenZFS daemon even when discovery hides Zed.

Return an error for unresolved Linux Zed launches instead of using the fallback. Preserve the fallback for other editors and platforms.

title: fix(server): cloning into a stranded clone project's empty folder reuses that project
author: juliusmarminge
head: ed1bd554b87a73e5fc7d4768fbb99eb8d1cf187e
body:
## Problem

When a clone fails or is cancelled, its project stays and its destination folder is left empty. Clone state lives only in memory, so after a server restart that project has no Retry, and every new clone into the same folder fails with **Failed to create clone project**. `prepareClone` accepts the empty folder, but `ProjectService.create` rejects the new project with `ProjectConflictError` because the earlier project still owns that workspace root.

Reproduced on main [4f0b74e190](https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/commit/4f0b74e190) in the web app with a fresh database:
1. Add project → Git URL with a repository that does not exist, into `…/projects/missing-repo`. Git fails and the folder is left empty.
2. Restart the server.
3. Clone `https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World.git` into the same folder.

Step 3 fails with "Failed to create clone project". The server trace matches the issue: `ProjectService.create` fails with `ProjectConflictError`, then `ProjectCloneTracker.start` fails. Without a restart, the same retry is refused with "already in progress" and the failed clone still offers Retry, so the restart is what strands the project.

## Change

- `ProjectCloneTracker.start` now handles `ProjectConflictError` from project creation by cloning for the project that owns the destination. It moves its in-memory claim to that project, launches the clone under its id, and returns that id. This only applies after `prepareClone` has accepted the destination as empty or [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Heavy lift**

**Gate project-ID substitution for older clients.**

This passthrough allows the tracker to return a different project ID. Older clients can continue waiting for the requested ID, so navigation or file copying can fail after the server reports success. Gate reuse on a client capability, or return a recoverable conflict to clients that do not advertise support. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/ed1bd554b87a73e5fc7d4768fbb99eb8d1cf187e/apps/server/src/project/ProjectCloneTracker.ts))

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Unarchive a reused project before opening it.**

An archived project can own the destination: `ProjectStore.findActiveByWorkspaceRoot` excludes deleted projects, not archived ones. This path opens that project without unarchiving it, so it remains absent from normal project navigation. The local-folder flow unarchives an existing project at Line 1874. Apply the same behavior for clone reuse, preferably across all clone callers. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/ed1bd554b87a73e5fc7d4768fbb99eb8d1cf187e/apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProjectStore.ts))

title: fix(web): trackpad flicks over the right panel tabs no longer navigate back
author: juliusmarminge
head: dc6715e7d120e9f5d02c5aa6f28f4997c5da8214
body:
## Problem

On desktop, a two-finger flick left over the right panel's overflowing tab strip navigates back once the tabs reach their left end, if the gesture still has momentum. The back indicator shows and the app leaves the current view, though the gesture began as tab scrolling.

The strip's wheel handler scrolled the tabs by hand and called `preventDefault()` on every wheel event while they moved. Chromium only starts a gesture scroll for wheel events the page does not consume, so `gestureScrollBegin`, which `HistorySwipeNavigation` uses to start tracking a new gesture, only fired when the strip hit its edge and stopped consuming. That reset the swipe tracker partway through the flick, and the remaining momentum was tracked as a fresh back swipe from the edge.

## Change

The tab strip now translates only vertical-dominant wheel input, such as a plain mouse wheel, into horizontal scrolling (the behaviour from https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/9461). Horizontal input returns early and scrolls the viewport natively. Chromium then begins the gesture scroll when the flick starts, and the swipe tracker ignores the whole gesture, as it already does for the diff and file panes. A swipe that starts at the strip's edge still navigates, like every other scroller.

Desktop forwards `gestureScrollBegin`/`gestureScrollEnd` over IPC, so a gesture's last wheel event can reach the renderer after its end. At the strip's left edge that straggler started a back swipe, left the indica [...]

title: fix(web): settings search shortcuts follow the physical key on non-US layouts
author: juliusmarminge
head: 016a3018578d7d4b8e6a77711c743e2640e4e4b1
body:
## Problem

In Settings, `/` and Cmd/Ctrl+F focus the search field only when the layout types exactly `/` or `f`. On a Russian or Ukrainian layout, the key next to right Shift (`code: "Slash"`) types `.`, and Ctrl/Cmd+F types `а` (`code: "KeyF"`). Neither shortcut does anything there, so focus stays where it was.

Reproduced on `main` (4f0b74e190) in the web dev server on `/settings/general`, by sending each layout's `key`/`code` pair as a keydown on the page body: US `/` and US Ctrl+F focus "Search settings"; Russian Slash and Russian Ctrl+F / Meta+F leave focus on the body.

## Change

The window keydown listener in `SettingsSidebarNav` now recognises both shortcuts with the shared `resolveEventKeys`, the same layout-then-physical-key fallback the configurable keybindings and `isRichTextBoldShortcut` use. Modifier rules, the editable-target and dialog exclusions, and the composition guard are unchanged.

- **Mod+F:** also matches the physical F key when the layout key is not a Latin letter. Dvorak and other Latin layouts keep using the key that types `f`.
- **`/`:** also matches the physical Slash key, unshifted. Shift still counts only when the layout itself types `/` with it (German Shift+7). Shift+Slash, which types `?` on US and `,` on Russian, still does nothing.

title: fix(web): MCP App cards no longer flash white in dark mode while the app loads
author: juliusmarminge
head: 7f2ac6d0e5a612d61b37ad14147d83badc21bdb1
body:
## Problem

In dark mode, MCP App cards on web and desktop are bright white blocks from the moment the frame loads until the app sends `ui/initialize`. For apps with a large bundle that is seconds. The `` gets `color-scheme: dark` from the host, but the app document has no color scheme until the theme bootstrap hears from the host, so Chromium paints the child canvas opaque white.

## Change

- `McpAppFrame` adds a `t3-color-scheme=` query parameter to the frame URL when it first adopts it. The frame still keeps that one URL; later theme changes keep flowing through `ui/notifications/host-context-changed`.

title: fix(server): fail Codex turns stuck in a provider retry
author: maria-rcks
head: 65f62fdb9b7d9ff6387ca68dbc4d3b860a57ddcf
body:
When Codex runs out of 429 reconnects it sometimes sends one more `error` with `willRetry: true` ("Reconnecting... 1/5", `exceeded retry limit, last status: 429 Too Many Requests`) and then never sends anything for that turn. The turn, its "Provider retry" row, and any `delegate_task` child stayed running forever, so the parent never heard back.

The Codex adapter now starts a 10 minute timer on each retry notice. If no model output or newer notice has replaced that retry by then, it fails the turn with the retry's failure and interrupts the native Codex turn. A retry whose last HTTP status is 429 fails as `usage_limit`, the same result as `responseTooManyFailedAttempts` at 429, so the child settles `failed` and the parent gets it through the existing subagent completion delivery.

I went with a timeout instead of treating the notice as terminal because the same payload does recover: in this machine's Codex logs, recovered retries resumed model output within about 75s, while the hung ones got nothing until a manual stop (8 are still open). Real transient disconnects that recover keep the current behavior: model output clears the retry and the timer does nothing.

The new adapter test replays the stuck transcript and fails on main by hanging. Server typecheck, lint, knip, and the orchestration-v2 tests pass. The finalize step rechecks the retry under the turn's terminalization permit, keeps a real `willRetry:false` failure, and leaves a turn alone when a user stop is already i [...]

title: fix(web): opening the terminal with Cmd+J no longer re-renders the whole sidebar
author: juliusmarminge
head: a3106d5f524fd7716291a95f7ab8713c4b431d39
body:
## Problem

Opening the terminal with Cmd/Ctrl+J got slower the more threads the sidebar held. Each press re-rendered the whole sidebar and every thread row several times: when Cmd/Ctrl went down, when the drawer opened, when the terminal took focus, and when it closed again. The sidebar subscribed to the held modifier keys, terminal focus and the current thread's `terminalOpen`, but only needed them for the thread-navigation shortcut context and the thread jump hints. Its row list isn't memoized, so each of those changes re-ran every row.

## Change

The sidebar now re-renders only when the thread jump hints actually appear or disappear.

- The thread-navigation keydown handler builds its `when` context when the key is pressed (`threadShortcutContext`). It reads terminal focus, the route thread's `terminalOpen`, preview focus, `previewOpen` and model-picker visibility directly, so custom `when` clauses see current values.
- `useThreadJumpHintsVisible(keybindings, routeThreadRef)` is a `useSyncExternalStore` with a boolean snapshot. The snapshot is true when the current modifier combination has been held unchanged for the existing hint delay and the hint conditions still match.

title: fix(server): updates copy the database while the server still runs when it cannot be cloned
author: binjamshid
head: 2743a1e6e9b67cc4003798d51c2c2dad1ff13c5a
body:
> [!WARNING]
> **This changes the update path, which is the most crash-critical code in T3 Code.** It copies a live SQLite database while the server is still writing to it, and its correctness rests on SQLite WAL locking rules and on a POSIX lock subtlety (below). It is tested and reviewed, but it has **not** run on real Linux ext4 hardware, on Windows, or inside the shipped single-executable `t3`. Please review it as a design change, not a small fix. I'm happy to close it if you'd rather keep the offline copy.

## Problem

On a filesystem that cannot clone files (Linux ext4, Windows NTFS), a service update stops the server and then copies the whole database before starting the new version, so the copy is all downtime. The reporter in #32952 has a 13.5 GB database on ext4 and sees about 3 minutes offline per update. The launcher their service runs (`v0.0.46`, pinned by #17490) and `main` both do this plain copy on ext4.

## Change

When the backup cannot be cloned, the launcher now copies the main database file **before** it stops the server:

1. After the update is accepted, the launcher opens a read-only `node:sqlite` connection and holds a read transaction. That keeps SQLite from resetting or truncating the WAL.
2. It copies the resolved main file with a `cp` child process (in-process `copyFile` on Windows) while the server keeps serving.
3. It stops the server, copies the WAL (not `-shm`), closes the snapshot, and renames staging into the normal backup directory.

The exi [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Set a busy timeout on the fake server's database connection to avoid a flaky test.**

The fake active child writes every 1 ms through `new DatabaseSync(paths.databasePath)`. `node:sqlite` uses a busy timeout of 0 by default. I did not run this test.

In the `delete` case, the launcher opens a read-only connection to the same file. That connection holds a SHARED lock while it reads `PRAGMA journal_mode`. If the child commits during that window, `insert.run` throws `SQLITE_BUSY` from the `setInterval` callback. The child then exits non-zero. `#handleExit` then throws "Active child exited unexpectedly", and the launcher fails before the backup is checked.

The window is short, but a 1 ms writer makes a collision possible. Give the child connection a busy timeout so the launcher's short read cannot crash it.

As per coding guidelines: "flaky tests are fixed, not retried."

_Source: Coding guidelines_

✅ Addressed in commit fe4bff9

replies.body: Fixed in fe4bff9814. The fake serving child now opens its connection with `{ timeout: 5000 }`, so a commit that lands while the launcher reads `journal_mode` waits for the lock instead of throwing `SQLITE_BUSY`. `serviceLauncher.test.ts` passes locally (18/18).

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

**Set the fake child’s busy timeout with a PRAGMA.**

On Node 23.11, `DatabaseSync` ignores `timeout`. In DELETE mode, the launcher’s schema read can overlap a write, causing the child to exit on `SQLITE_BUSY` and the test to fail. Set the timeout through SQLite so the writer can wait for the reader.

✅ Confirmed as addressed by @binjamshid

title: fix(web): mouse tilt wheel no longer switches threads on Windows and Linux desktop
author: juliusmarminge
head: 761926fa7679c69fa6581da21ab1415e0ae72cb6
body:
## Problem

On the Windows desktop app, tilting a mouse wheel over anything without a horizontal scroller (chat, left sidebar, right sidebar) shows the swipe arrow and switches to the previous or next thread. `HistorySwipeNavigation` treats every pixel-mode wheel stream that is mostly horizontal as a two-finger trackpad swipe.

Reproduced on the Linux desktop app (Electron 44, Xvfb) with real X11 tilt-wheel input. After visiting two threads, one tilt-left tick over the chat arrives as a single wheel event, `deltaX=-120 deltaMode=0`, and navigates back. A tilt-right tick navigates forward, and a tilt over the sidebar navigates too. A vertical wheel does nothing. Electron's main-process `input-event` brackets this mouse-wheel stream with `gestureScrollBegin`/`gestureScrollEnd`, exactly like a trackpad gesture, and reports only `{type, modifiers}`. So on Windows and Linux, neither the renderer nor the main process can tell a discrete mouse wheel from a trackpad.

## Change

`HistorySwipeNavigation` now attaches its wheel and gesture listeners only on macOS (`isMacPlatform(navigator.platform)`). Its gesture model is macOS's: it detects when the fingers lift from the momentum tail and from Chromium's gesture brackets. On Windows and Linux, horizontal wheel input goes back to plain scrolling. Back/forward stays available there through the sidebar buttons and the keyboard shortcuts. Two-finger swipe navigation is therefore macOS-only; behaviour on macOS is unchanged.

title: fix(cli): installers retry transient GitHub errors
author: juliusmarminge
head: c9182125243d15181a697fa190aad7efb64f10b1
body:
## Problem

When github.com answers a release request with a transient error, every CLI install path gives up on the first one. During the current GitHub degradation, about half of github.com requests return HTTP 504 after ~11 s (seen for `cli/cli` too). title: fix(client-runtime): pasted repository page URLs clone the repository into its own folder
author: juliusmarminge
head: 8a23cc7c3507047b92aa52c5460fce637c71ad5e
body:
## Problem

Pasting a repository page URL copied from the browser, such as `https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/tree/main`, into **Add project → Git URL** sent that page URL to `git clone` unchanged. The suggested destination was named after the branch (`~/main`). The clone then failed with `fatal: repository 'https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/tree/main/' not found` and left an empty `main` folder behind. The same happens with GitLab `/-/tree/`, Forgejo/Codeberg `/src/branch/`, GitCafe `/tree/` and GitHub `/blob//` pages. Bitbucket `/src//` pages do clone, but into a folder named after the ref.

## Change

- Each source control definition can map its own repository page URLs back to the repository URL through a new optional `repositoryUrlFromPage(url, known)`, following the existing per-host `parseCommitUrl(url, known)` pattern. Routes:

  - GitLab: everything before the first `/-/`.
  - Forgejo/Gitea: `src/branch|tag|commit`, on hosts Forgejo recognizes (codeberg.org, `forgejo.*`, `gitea.*`). A Forgejo path ending in `.git` is always a clone URL, since Forgejo can be mounted below any path.
  - Bitbucket: `src/`, on Bitbucket hosts only.
- The registry asks the definition that recognizes the URL's host, so another host's any-host route never rewrites a recognized host's URL.
- On a host no definition recognizes:

  - A Forgejo-shaped `src/branch/…` path is left alone, b [...]

title: fix(shared): login-shell environment probe ignores DEBUG trap output
author: juliusmarminge
head: 8457e471063eec552be8e44e79bf309c1925b19d
body:
## Problem

T3 Code reads environment variables such as `PATH` and `XDG_DATA_HOME` by running the login shell with `-ilc` and printing each value between `__T3CODE_ENV__START__` / `_END__` markers. A common `.bashrc` snippet that shows the running command in the terminal title, `trap 'echo -ne "\033]0;${BASH_COMMAND}\007"' DEBUG`, echoes every probe command to stdout before it runs, markers included. The parser then reads the trap's output as the value. In the report, `XDG_DATA_HOME` came back as `'\a__T3CODE_ENV_XDG_DATA_HOME_START__\n\e]0;printenv XDG_DATA_HOME\a…`, and "Update all" ran `claude update` with it, which rewrote `~/.local/bin/claude` into a broken symlink. `PATH` is corrupted the same way.

Reproduced on main with bash 5.2: a profile containing that trap, `XDG_DATA_HOME` unset, then `readEnvironmentFromLoginShell("/bin/bash", ["XDG_DATA_HOME", "PATH"])`. The returned `XDG_DATA_HOME` is exactly the corrupt prefix of the reporter's symlink target (the target is that value plus `/claude/versions/`).

## Change

`buildEnvironmentCaptureCommand` now starts the probe with `(trap - DEBUG) 2>/dev/null && trap - DEBUG;` when the shell's basename is `bash`, `zsh`, `sh`, `ksh` or `ksh93`, so a DEBUG trap is cleared before any marker is printed. The reset is tried in a subshell first because OpenBSD ksh (loksh, oksh; also OpenBSD's `/bin/sh`) exits on `trap - DEBUG` even with `|| true`; there the subshell fails and the probe runs as before. Other shells (dash, mksh, fish,  [...]

** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

The Test check captures `/usr/bin:/bin:/snap/bin` instead of `shellPath` and fails. Bash reads `/etc/profile` first, which can change `HOME` before it reads the fixture. Load the fixture explicitly in the injected subprocess before the capture command so the test installs the DEBUG trap reliably.

✅ Addressed in commit 1e836dc

The test no longer runs a login shell: it runs the probe command with non-interactive `bash -c` and `BASH_ENV` pointing at the test's own file, which installs PATH and the DEBUG trap. In that mode bash reads no /etc/profile, /etc/profile.d or /etc/bash.bashrc (checked with strace). It still fails against main's shell.ts and passes with the fix.

title: fix(server): a follow-up delegated task waits for a run its child queued on its own thread
author: juliusmarminge
head: b30f5090b5cb177412b650ea1cda3ba46119e772
body:
## Problem

When a parent sends a finished delegated child a follow-up and the child queues a continuation on its own thread (`t3_thread_send` to itself, `mode: "queue"`), the follow-up task settled on the turn that queued the continuation ("HANDOFF-C"). The continuation's reply ("FINAL-D") never reached the parent as the task result. The original task already waits for such a run. Reproduced on main with a real Claude provider: the follow-up task's result was `HANDOFF-C`.

## Change

- A run that a thread queues for itself now takes the `delegatedTaskId` of the thread's active run, the same way restart continuations already inherit theirs (`continuedTaskId` in `Orchestrator.ts`). The follow-up's latest run is then the continuation, so the task stays pending until that run finishes and settles on its reply.
- Follow-up result selection (finalization, the pending check, and `task_status`) goes through one helper, `delegatedTaskResultRun`. Like the original task, it passes over a queued continuation that was removed before it started or is held in the queue, as long as an earlier run of the task started. Without this, removing or holding the continuation would cancel the follow-up or leave it running. It prefers the run still executing, then a queued one, over the latest finished one. That way a waiting continuation does not make the task read as queued while its turn is running, and a reordered queue cannot settle the task while an older continuation still waits.

An unbound scheduled task that the user switched to «Use the project checkout» in Settings is reset to «Create a new worktree» as soon as an agent updates it over MCP with `bindToCurrentThread: false`, even though the task was never bound. title: fix(web): Word previews no longer cut ordinary documents short
author: yaacovcorcos
head: b2e5156f3ceef65122218f7c76d5f7465991532b
body:
## Problem

A Word preview stops at the first long table, and long documents lose their style and list definitions. A report with a 300-row table previews as one page, with "Preview limited", and nothing from the table on. Fixes #32039.

## Change

`officeArchive.ts` bounds a Word file before `@betteroffice/docx` opens it. The old bounds were sized for a renderer on the page's main thread, but the engine lays out in its own worker. The limits now sit in one `WORD_LIMITS` table, and each was measured against the engine (Apple silicon, in the worker):

| Limit | Was | Now | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Do not discard a whole prose text node when it contains an unrelated escape.**

An escape elsewhere in the node makes `raw` differ from `node.value`, so the guard at line 47 returns before any path in that node is matched. For example, `See \* and /tmp/notes.md` parses to one text node, and `/tmp/notes.md` is skipped and stays plain text. The Windows-path escape plugin does not change this input, because it only rewrites escapes that follow an unfinished drive path.

Map each path match in `node.value` back to its source offsets, and create edits only for those spans. The guard should not reject the entire node. A direct `absoluteFilePathMatches(raw)` on the source slice is not a safe substitute, because it can include escape backslashes inside a path.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Reject ellipses in every path segment.**

The `textMustNot` pattern only matches ellipses immediately after `/tmp/claude-1000/`. A response containing the required full link and an abbreviated segment such as `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-user--t3.../scratchpad/notes.md` can pass this case. Match ellipses anywhere in an emitted path token.

---

** Minor** · **Maintainability & Code Quality** · **Quick win**

**Add a control case for ordinary work.**

This file adds only a `"kind": "bad"` case. Add a control case where the correct response does not contain a file link. This catches an over-correction that emits file links for unrelated requests.

As per coding guidelines: “Add controls: cases where the correct action is ordinary work.” As per path instructions: “Add controls: cases where the correct action is ordinary work.”

_Sources: Coding guidelines, Path instructions_

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Exclude unmatched closing brackets from path matches.**

For `See [ /tmp/notes.md]`, the matcher includes `]` in the path, so the link points to `/tmp/notes.md]`. It also accepts `/tmp/cache/...]` as a file path instead of rejecting the abbreviated path. Preserve balanced brackets in filenames, but exclude unmatched closing brackets. Add both cases to the existing tests.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Reject links rendered as inline code.**

A response that puts `[name](/tmp/claude-1000/.../notes.md)` inside backticks can satisfy `textMust`, but Markdown renders it as code rather than a usable link. The grader applies this pattern directly to the response text. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/3bf1cfac636a2c36e613b7912dda27b372017183/evals/mcp-tool-use/run.ts)) Check for a rendered Markdown link node instead.

## Problem

A merged GitLab merge request had no "Revert changes" action. GitHub's revert opens a pull request through `revertPullRequest`, but the GitLab provider never offered `revert`. Closes #30555.

## Change

GitLab has no single "revert this merge request" endpoint, so the CLI does what GitLab's Revert button does, in three REST calls:

1. Create `revert-` from the target branch.
2. Revert the merge commit onto it with `POST repository/commits/:sha/revert`. GitLab picks the mainline parent for a merge commit and writes "This reverts merge request !N" into the commit message.
3. Open a merge request `Revert ""` into the target branch, with the source branch removed on merge.

The commit to revert is the merge commit, or the squash commit for a squashed fast-forward merge. A fast-forward merge without squash landed as several commits and has no single commit to revert, so it fails with a message that says so.

If GitLab can't revert cleanly (a conflict, or the change was already reverted), the new branch is deleted so a retry doesn't hit "branch already exists". GitLab's own reason ("It may have already been done, or a more recent commit may have updated some of this content") reaches the user.

`revert` joins the actions that `user.can_merge` gates, since it pushes a branch to the target project. Web and mobile already show the action for a merged change request, so they needed no change.

## Verification

- New tests in `GitLabPullRequestCli.test.ts [...]

title: fix(gitlab): review comments can cover a range of lines
author: TonybynMp4
head: 9347349ce5dd9f0788c2a5d2e1cd74649993f23f
body:
## Problem

On GitLab merge requests, a review comment could only cover one line. The provider didn't declare `review.rangeComment`, and `submitReview` sent no `line_range`. Closes #30534.

## Change

- The GitLab provider now declares `review.rangeComment: true`, so the web diff offers the same range selection it does for GitHub.
- When a draft has a `startPosition`, `submitReview` adds `position.line_range` with both ends. Each end carries `type` (`new`, `old`, or null for a context line), its line numbers, and a `line_code` of `sha1(path)_old_new`.
- GitLab's diff parser fills the missing side of an added or removed line with a counter that only the diff knows. I send 0 there. GitLab reads only the `line_code` side that matches `type`, and its own header shows the range right ("Comment on lines +1 to +3"). gitlab.com also accepts a range with no `line_code`, but older frontends parse the header from it, so I kept it.
- A one-line range sends no `line_range`, same as before.
- The hash uses `effect/crypto/Digest`, as the package's Effect diagnostics ask.

Mobile has no range selection yet, and T3's thread view still shows a ranged comment on its last line, because `PullRequestReviewThread` has no start line. Both are true for GitHub today too, so I left them alone.

## Scope and approval

GitLab adapter only. No contract or client change. Tracked in #30534.

## Verification

- The `submitReview` test now posts a range from a context line to an added line [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Heavy lift**

**Build line codes from the diff’s line counters.**

For an added line in a modified file, GitLab retains the preceding old-line counter. Line `+12` can therefore have a code ending in `_10_12`, not `_0_12`. The same problem applies to the new-line counter of a deleted line. GitLab looks up range endpoints by these codes, so the submitted range can fail to identify its selected lines. Obtain both counters from the diff before building each code. Add a modified-file case to the existing submission test. ([gitlab.com](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/raw/master/lib/gitlab/diff/parser.rb))

✅ Addressed in commit a4cd1ba

The submission test now covers a renamed, modified file where line +12 follows a removed line and gets `_11_12`. If the diff cannot be read, it fal [...]

@TonybynMp4 The supplied code addresses the line-counter issue. `gitLabLineCounters` reads both counters from the hunk, and `gitLabLineRangeEnd` uses them to build `line_code`.

The fallback preserves review submission when the diff read fails, but range highlighting remains best-effort in that case. I have not rerun the submission test.

`gitLabLineRangeEnd` sends `type: null` for a context endpoint. The GitLab Discussions API documents `position[line_range][start][type]` and `position[line_range][end][type]` as `new` for added lines and `old` otherwise. author: fedeinfe
head: bd8978c2ce8333651c9abf2896399140df6c23ce
body:
When a user answers an agent's question with "show me the reference", the agent opens the images and asks again. The images only exist inside the collapsed tool group, so the user sees "I examined the mockups" and nothing to look at.

Each tool group now keeps a thumbnail strip of the images it opened, right below the group, on web and mobile. Clicking or tapping a thumbnail opens the existing full-size preview.

## Summary

```diff
 deriveMessagesTimelineRows (web) / appendActivityGroupRows (mobile)
   work-live | work | work-toggle        "Read 2 files"
     (expanded group details)
+  viewed-images                         paths = workEntriesViewedImagePaths(group entries)
```

- `workEntriesViewedImagePaths` (client-runtime) collects the distinct `viewedImagePath` of a group's entries, in viewing order. Both clients use it.
- Web renders the strip with `ChatMarkdownAssetImage` (max height 10rem, `onImageExpand`). Mobile shows two per line through the existing `renderViewedImage`.
- A settled turn's "Worked for…" fold still hides its work, strip included, until it is opened.
- Providers: nothing provider-specific was added. Any adapter that reports an image read gets the strip; Claude sets `viewedImagePath` on `Read`.
- Not covered: images an MCP tool returns as output, such as Figma `get_screenshot` with base64. Their output is left off the wire (`outputOmitted`), so showing them needs a contract change. When Claude saves those screenshots and `Read`s them, which is what h [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Resolve workspace images in mobile previews.**

A preview such as `![Sidebar](mock.png)` cannot load an image from the thread workspace. `QuestionText` supplies no workspace image resolver, so the native renderer has no way to fetch it from the environment. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/357297196c08336966d2c6a820d6d4e4f255c20f/apps/mobile/src/native/EnrichedMarkdownText.tsx))

Pass the thread and workspace context and reuse `useMarkdownImageSource`, as `FileMarkdownPreview` does. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/357297196c08336966d2c6a820d6d4e4f255c20f/apps/mobile/src/features/files/FileMarkdownPreview.tsx))

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Preserve whitespace in preview Markdown.**

Trimming removes the leading indentation from an indented code block. For example, `    first\n    second` renders as prose rather than code. ([spec.commonmark.org](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/))

Use `trim()` only to check whether the preview is empty, then render the original string. Apply the same fix in `apps/mobile/src/features/threads/PendingUserInputCard.tsx` at Line 250.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Keep thumbnail width non-negative.**

When a split-layout feed first renders with `contentWidth` at zero, this calculation produces `-4`. The new row then supplies a negative width to each image container. Clamp the width to zero until the viewport is measured. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/03456727e7d393f2a2a469973005e86ec7e18dc1/apps/mobile/src/features/threads/ThreadFeed.tsx))

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Create viewed-image rows for failed runs.**

When a run fails after an image read, `deriveThreadFeedPresentation` sends its activity groups directly to the result. It never reaches this collector, so mobile shows no preview outside the work row. Add image rows to the failed-run path as well. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/03456727e7d393f2a2a469973005e86ec7e18dc1/apps/mobile/src/lib/threadActivity.ts))

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Include image reads in the itemized failed-run path.**

When a run fails after an image read, `itemizedRunIds` sends that read through the earlier single-work-row branch. The branch continues before this call, so the preview is absent outside the work row. Emit a viewed-image row for qualifying reads in that branch. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/03456727e7d393f2a2a469973005e86ec7e18dc1/apps/web/src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.logic.ts))

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Keep `#` and `%` in viewed image paths literal.**

`viewedImagePath` stores the Codex `imageView` path unchanged. Web and mobile both pass it to `resolveViewedImageAsset`, which parses it as a Markdown destination. For a path with `#`, the thumbnail resolves to the text before the `#`. For a path with `%XX`, the thumbnail can resolve to a different file.

- `/workspace/C#/mock.png` resolves to `/workspace/C`. A `?` causes the same truncation.
- `/workspace/a%20b.png` resolves to `/workspace/a b.png`.

A `%` without two hex digits stays literal.

Encoding the stored value as a file URL would skip the Markdown parsing for this path. That value also feeds the read gate in `MessagesTimeline.logic.ts`, the detail comparison in `TimelineWorkEntryRow.logic.ts`, and the output formatting in `itemDetail.ts`. Check those consumers before changing the value. Changing `markdownDestinationHostPath` changes every Markdown destination, so a resolver change should apply only to viewed-image paths.

Add a regression case with a native path that contains `#` and a literal `%` followed by two hex digits.

title: fix(client-runtime): a search query pasted from github.com lists pull requests again
author: juliusmarminge
head: e80707f14be33e17101cd43646567e1410c0b452
body:
## Problem

A search query copied from github.com, for example `is:pr state:open -draft:true repo:org/repo author:alice author:bob`, lists no pull requests. `parsePullRequestQuery` reads `is:`, `state:` and `repo:` as required labels, so no PR can match. It leaves `-draft:true` in the free text, which is sent to the host as one literal phrase. Of two `author:` qualifiers it keeps only the last, without telling the user.

Reproduced on `main` (cefb544af3) in the web dev server against pingdotgg/t3code: that query, `is:pr is:open repo:pingdotgg/t3code author:juliusmarminge` and `-draft:true author:juliusmarminge` all show "Nothing matches". `author:juliusmarminge` alone lists 99+ open PRs.

## Change

All changes are in `parsePullRequestQuery` (`packages/client-runtime/src/pullRequestQuery.ts`), the parser shared by web and mobile:

- **GitHub's own search terms are ignored.** `is:`, `state:`, `archived:`, `repo:`, `org:`, `user:` and `sort:`, with or without a leading `-`, now become neither labels nor text. The list's own controls already set its scope, state and order. `archived:` is included because the github.com Pull Requests dashboard adds `archived:false` to every query it builds.
- **Other unknown keys are still labels.** A key not in that list is still read as a scoped label, so `size:XXL` and `area:web` keep working.
- **Negated draft.** `-draft:true` now hides drafts, and `-draft:false` shows only drafts.
- **Several authors.** The filter contract holds one author,  [...]

** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Preserve the requested author union.**

For `author:alice author:bob`, this removes the author filter. The provider then accepts PRs by any author, rather than only Alice or Bob. This does not meet the linked issue’s expected result. ([github.com](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/30131))

Carry multiple authors through the filter contract and provider as an OR condition. Update the existing author test to assert that behavior.

That is a capability, not part of this fix. The issue's expected result allows ignoring an unsupported qualifier, so two different authors now drop the typed author filter instead of silently  [...]
