title: fix(server): t3 doctor warns how long reclaiming takes and shows each step
author: juliusmarminge
head: d94de3083c311c4ee76d15a7077a540d6ad64ba3
body:
## Problem

`t3 doctor`'s "Reclaim database space" repair kept the reporter's background service down for 72 minutes on a 12.8 GB database. Before running it said "This can take several minutes...", and then it printed nothing until `Done`, so a long run looked the same as a hung one. Reproduced on main with a synthetic 1.59 GiB database (`auto_vacuum = NONE`, like installs that predate incremental vacuum). After that line the output stayed silent for 36.6 s. On that synthetic database, temporary per-step timing put most of the time in `VACUUM`, a full rewrite of the file: 26 s at 1.59 GiB and 77 s at 3.18 GiB. The event-store scan took 5–10 s.

## Change

- `DatabaseMaintenance.compact` takes an optional `onStep` callback and calls it as each step starts: verify, compact events, verify, vacuum, rebuild search, checkpoint.
- Before the prompt, the doctor repair description names the database size and warns that the repair rewrites the whole database, which can take more than an hour on a large database or slow disk.
- While the service is stopped, doctor prints one line per step with the elapsed time (`[m:ss]`, on the monotonic clock) and the total time on the `Done` line. It no longer promises "several minutes".
- `docs/user/background-service.md` now says the time grows with the size of the whole database and can exceed an hour, instead of "several minutes".

The repair's SQL and step order are unchanged.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#29941

title: fix(server): t3 service install works on Linux hosts without a login session
author: juliusmarminge
head: 6d21c45dc4d54931a18e72537c1593a1003ed8ec
body:
## Problem

On a Linux host where the T3 user has no logind session (a Coder workspace, a container reached through `docker exec --user`, a shell without PAM), `t3 service install` stopped right away with `[user-manager-unavailable]`. Two things caused it. The systemd commands inherited a shell with no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, so `systemctl --user` could not find the user bus even when the manager was running. And the install never tried the unprivileged `loginctl enable-linger`, which is what starts `user@` on such a host.

Reproduced on main 689bdb82e9 in a Debian 13 container with systemd as PID 1, as user `tester` through `docker exec --user` (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` empty, `loginctl show-user` reporting "not logged in or lingering"). The install failed, and afterwards Linger was still unset and `user@1000` was inactive.

## Change

All in `apps/server/src/cloud/bootService.ts`:

- On Linux, when the installer has no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, the boot service's subprocesses get `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/`. It is read through `Config`, like `HOME` and `PATH`.
- The prerequisite check runs `loginctl enable-linger --no-ask-password ` in two cases: when lingering is disabled (as before), and when logind does not know the user yet and the user manager is down. It then re-checks for the manager for up to about 5 seconds (10 × 500 ms), because lingering starts it asynchronously.
- If lingering started the manager, the install re-reads the manager's unit directory. A shell `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` that d [...]

**Exclude root under sudo from the runtime-directory fallback.**

When `uid === 0` and `SUDO_USER` is set, the fallback points `busctl --user` and `systemctl --user` at `/run/user/0`. If a root user manager is available, installation can write and activate a separate root `t3code.service`. The base implementation did not reach this installation path with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` unset. This violates the existing sudo contract and can leave the normal user's service uninstalled.

✅ Addressed in commit a66d091

**Enforce a deadline for manager startup.**

If a `systemctl --user` probe takes its five-second timeout, this loop can make an initial probe and ten repeats before it fails. title: fix(server): long Claude sessions import instead of being skipped
author: juliusmarminge
head: aa634aafc78d98330e82934b496580294ec298e8
body:
## Problem

Importing Claude Code sessions skips long sessions. The server logs `Could not read imported transcript … Transcript selected history exceeds the 32 MiB memory budget` and the session counts as skipped. The read kept every conversational record in memory, but the import only shows the first user message and the latest messages. The JSON reader also charges about 4 bytes per character of text, so on current main a session is skipped once its conversation text reaches roughly 8 MiB. Reproduced on main by running `AgentSessionScanner.recentThreads` on a synthetic Claude transcript with 600 messages of 64 KiB (37.6 MiB file): the result was `Skipped`.

When reading a Claude transcript, the scanner keeps only the first user message plus a rolling window of the latest 200 conversational records. title: fix(server): Git failures no longer record checkpoints as missing
author: juliusmarminge
head: 9d3e315a6db6db5b8029bb613184513647aa16d5
body:
## Problem

When Git fails on a project (for example `fatal: bad config line 1 in file .git/config`, exit 128), the repository probes read the failure as "not a repository" and the checkpoint ref lookup reads it as "ref absent". The turn's checkpoints are then recorded as `missing` with no files, identical to a folder without Git, so the changed files and the rewind snapshot disappear without any sign of why.

Reproduced on main with the reporter's steps: register a fresh `git init` repo, write `invalid config` into its `.git/config`, run a devReplay turn. Both checkpoints were `missing` and the server logged nothing.

## Change

- `GitVcsDriver`: `isInsideWorkTree` and `detectRepository` share one probe that returns "no work tree" only when Git says so (a `fatal: not a git repository` or `fatal: cannot use bare repository` line, stdout `false` from Git before 2.38, or a cwd that no longer exists), read line by line under `LC_ALL=C` so trace output and warnings cannot hide it. Any other failure raises `VcsProcessExitError`.
- `resolveCheckpointCommit`: `rev-parse --verify --quiet` exiting 1 still means the ref is absent, unless Git also reports an `error:` or `fatal:` line (an unreadable object); any other exit raises.
- `VcsDriverRegistry` reads only that probe failure as "no repository", so Git status, review, source control and the clients behave as before for a repository Git cannot open.
- `CheckpointStore.isGitRepository` asks the Git driver again when the registry find [...]

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Make the included-config case read its included file on Windows.**

On Windows, `path.join(includeDir, "included")` puts backslashes into the Git config value. Git interprets backslashes as escapes. Git can therefore reject the config before it reads the included file, while all three failure assertions still pass. Write the include path with forward slashes and confirm that Git reads the included file. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config/2.36.2.html?utm_source=openai))

title: fix(server): listing linked environments no longer waits out an asleep peer
author: juliusmarminge
head: 8f8df99e0fea54dc34f1c77c848ccb9cdfab2c63
body:
## Problem

`peerLinks.list` (Settings → Linked environments, `t3_environment_links`, `t3 environment list`) probed each linked environment's addresses one after another, and each probe could wait 10 s on a non-loopback route. One sleeping laptop held the whole list for 10 s per address. Reproduced on main 7195b69954 with two servers from the checkout, environment A linked to peer B over two Tailscale addresses, and B frozen with SIGSTOP: `t3 environment list` took 3.0 s with B awake, 13.0 s with one address and 23.1 s with two. About 3.0 s of every run is CLI startup.

## Change

`statusOf` in `apps/server/src/peer/PeerLinks.ts` now probes all of a link's addresses at once and counts the link reachable as soon as one answers as that environment. The race is capped at 3 s, the budget loopback already uses, and a link that has not answered by then lists as unreachable. `resolve`, `link` and `describe` keep `probeTimeout`, so a real call to a waking machine still gets its 10 s. No contract, stored state or client changes.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#28531

title: fix(server): say Git isn't installed when a new project can't run git
author: juliusmarminge
head: 860925bddea28d715b054a68d187f64df4a48405
body:
## Problem

Creating a new project on a machine without Git failed with "Could not create the project / Failed to create the project folder." and never said Git was missing. Repro: start the server with no `git` on PATH, then Command palette → New project → "T3Code Test" → Create. The server's `git init` fails with `GitCommandError: Failed to spawn Git process.`, and `createNamedProject` replaces that with the fixed folder message.

## Change

`NamedProjectFolderError.message` now checks its cause. When the cause is a `GitCommandError` whose spawn failed with `NotFound`, the message is "Git isn't installed on this machine. Install Git to create a project." Every other failure keeps "Failed to create the project folder.", and the folder is still removed on failure.

The spawner checks the working directory with `fs.access` before it spawns, so a missing folder fails as `FileSystem.access` NotFound. That is how the check tells a missing folder apart from a missing executable. Web and desktop toasts, the mobile error banner and the MCP `t3_project_create` tool already show this error's `message`, so no client or contract changes.

## Problem

Expanding unchanged lines in a diff can throw `DiffHunksRenderer.processDiffResult: deletionLine and additionLine are null, something is wrong` or `trailing context mismatch`. On a working-tree diff in the web app, expanding context while an agent kept editing the files took the whole app to the root error screen within a minute.

The patch was computed earlier, but expanding loads each file as it is now. `@pierre/diffs` hydrates the partial patch with those contents without checking them. When the file has changed since, the hydrated diff's hunks no longer fit its lines.

## Change

- `createDiffFileContentsLoader` (`apps/web/src/lib/diffFileContents.ts`), shared by the diff panel and the PR loaders, now rejects contents that no longer reproduce the patch it was asked to load. Each hunk must fit in the loaded files with matching lines, and the unchanged tail must be the same length on both sides. Lines are compared ignoring whitespace, because the Changes panel's ignore-whitespace patches print context lines from one side only.
- Pierre already catches loader errors, so the file keeps showing its patch, and expanding works again once the diff refreshes.
- PR guide excerpts (`GuideExcerpt.logic.ts`) now load with their source file's diff, so the check runs against the real patch. They then build the excerpt's old side as before. title: fix(server): closed PR watches end even when the activity read fails
author: juliusmarminge
head: eefcaf1fb7d7b01b86cadd400bdd89abf596f1d9
body:
## Problem

A PR watch reads the pull request's detail and activity together, and any failure counts as a failed read. When the PR was closed but its activity read kept failing, the closed detail was never acted on. After 8 failed reads the watch stopped and told the agent to "call watch_pull_request to watch it again". The agent re-armed the closed PR, and the cycle repeated dozens of times until someone called `unwatch_pull_request`.

Reproduced with a test against the real reactor and orchestration runtime, using a mocked host whose `detail` returns a closed PR and whose `activity` fails. On main the watch ends with `#8: stopped watching, could not read it`, not `#8: closed, stopped watching`.

## Change

- `readGroup` in `PullRequestWatchReactor.ts` still runs both reads at once, but it keeps the activity result as an `Exit`. If detail says the PR is closed or merged, the activity result is ignored and the existing closed/merged ending runs. For an open PR, an activity failure is re-raised with its original cause, so rate-limit pausing and the eight-failure limit behave as before.
- The give-up notice now ends with "call watch_pull_request only if it is still open". When T3 cannot read detail at all, it cannot tell whether the PR is closed, so the agent should only re-arm after checking.

The eight-failure limit (https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/18894) is unchanged. Watching a PR whose cached snapshot says closed is still allowed (https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

**Preserve an activity rate-limit that completes before detail fails.**

When `plan.activity` is enabled, `Effect.exit` converts the activity failure into a successful value. If activity returns a rate-limit before detail fails, the later detail failure prevents the `Effect.flatMap` from exposing that activity result. The watch then counts the detail failure, and repeated co-failures can reach the eight-failure give-up path.

Record the completed activity failure without joining the activity after detail fails. Keep detail’s current fail-fast behavior.

replies.body: Not changing this. On main, a co-failure already paused or counted depending on which read failed first, so this case was order-dependent before. Here a detail read that fails without a rate limit is a real failure for the watch: the detail is the read it needs, so counting it toward the eight-failure limit is correct. When detail itself is rate-limited, `isRateLimited(read.cause)` still pauses as [...]

@juliusmarminge You're right. I treated the previous order-dependent pause as a required behavior without evidence. The detail failure should follow its own failure classification; an activity rate limit does not need to override it. The mutable slot is unnecessary. I withdraw this finding.

---

** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

**Require activity-read recovery before re-arming.**

An open pull request with a persistent activity-read failure can be re-armed through `watch_pull_request`. The watch then reaches the same eight-failure give-up path again. Make the notice require both an open pull request and confirmed recovery of activity reads.

** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

author: juliusmarminge

## Problem

While a turn streams, providers that send `message.updated` on every tick (ACP agents including the dev Replay provider, Cursor, OpenCode) give the client's thread projection a new `messages` array each tick. title: fix(server): a steer during a delegate_task wait no longer drops the child's result
author: juliusmarminge
head: 436e068559267958431b2ddb087e14b4fe349fea
body:
## Problem

A parent that calls `delegate_task` with `mode: "wait"` loses the child's result if the user steers it during the wait and its turn is still running when the child finishes. The steer cancels the tool call, which ends the wait without a `taskId`. The task stays at `completionWake: "settled_only"`. The orchestrator then skips delivery while the parent run is live, and nothing delivers the result after that run settles. The task row ends as `completed | settled_only | completionDelivery: null`, the same row the issue reports.

Reproduced on main `a773dc38ac` in the web dev server with a Claude Sonnet 5.5 parent:
1. The parent calls `delegate_task` (mode `wait`). The child is Claude Haiku 5.5 and sleeps 25 s.
2. While the row shows "Delegating", steer the parent to run a 60 s command.
3. The child completes while the steered turn is still running. That turn ends with `STEER-DONE`, and `CHILD-DONE-27362` never reaches the parent.

## Change

The blocking wait now lives in one place, `awaitTask`, which the local and remote (linked environment) wait paths both call. The switch to `completionWake: "always"` used to run only when the wait returned without a terminal result (a timeout). It now also runs from an `Effect.onExit` finalizer when the wait fails or its fiber is interrupted, which is what a cancelled MCP `tools/call` does. The finalizer runs uninterruptibly. It uses the same `delegated_task.wake-policy` command and the same command ids as before.

That command al [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

**Make the `Effect.onExit` finalizer decide every upgrade.**

1. The `upgradeWake` decision is split across two places. The `Effect.onExit` finalizer handles failure and interruption. The explicit `yield* upgradeWake` at Line 1654 handles a successful wait with no terminal result.
2. Assume `waitForTask` succeeds with `Option.none()` (timeout) or with a non-terminal result. The finalizer then runs `Effect.void`.
3. Assume the MCP `tools/call` is cancelled at that moment, after `waitForTask` returns but before Line 1654 starts. The fiber is interrupted at the generator step boundary, so the explicit upgrade never runs.
4. The task then keeps `completionWake: "settled_only"`. The child result does not reach the live parent run, which is the bug this PR fixes.

The trigger is narrow: the timeout and the cancellation must happen at almost the same time. The fix is small. Put the full decision in the finalizer. The finalizer runs uninterruptibly, so the upgrade happens exactly once, and the explicit call can go.

title: fix(client-runtime): server updates stop waiting 32 minutes when the host returns without this update's outcome
author: juliusmarminge
head: 183bebc70a142d6590e3d9b9ff9a6eb053d14a3a
body:
## Problem

After a launcher (`boot-service`) server update, the client waits only for a `ready` event that carries this update's `updateOutcome`. If the host comes back as a server the launcher did not start for this update, every `ready` is dropped. That happens, for example, when an SSH route's `t3 serve` takes the T3 home during the restart, or after a manual `t3 update`, which has its own update id. The status bar then shows "Restarting…" for the full 32-minute `SERVER_UPDATE_RESUME_TIMEOUT` while the host is in normal use.

Reproduced on main by driving the real update command (`createServerEnvironmentAtoms` → `updateServer`) with a fake environment registry on `TestClock`:
1. The update is accepted with `updateId: "update-1"`.
2. The old process replays its `ready`.
3. A new process sends a `ready` with no outcome, or with another update's outcome.

A minute later the state is still `running / resuming`.

## Change

The client now tells server processes apart by `ready.payload.at`. The server publishes this once per process at startup, and the lifecycle subscription replays it unchanged.

- **Record the accepting process.** On `boot-service` hosts, before sending the update request, the client reads the current process's `ready.at`, waiting at most 5 s. It keeps it only if the update request goes out on the same RPC session that the `ready` came from.
- **End the wait on a different process.** During the resume wait, a `ready` with a different `at` ends the wait. The e [...]

** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Bind `acceptedAt` and the update RPC to one session.**

`bindAcceptedAt` reads session S1, but `request` and `runStream` call `currentSession()` again. If the supervisor reconnects to S2 between those reads, an S2 `ready` replay can end the resume wait. Validation then records a failed terminal update because S2 has no committed outcome for this update. This is an incorrect update result, not an unavailable-service failure.

Pass the acquired `RpcSession` through both update paths instead of reacquiring it.

The foreign rollback reason can be checked in the existing `correlates launcher outcomes` validation test; the foreign-commit case already exercises the resume path. Could you move this assertion there and remove this full orchestration test?

title: fix(server): runs cancelled by a server restart say why in the thread
author: juliusmarminge
head: cabafde0cc81e20531d10fb1d852d897d556a94b
body:
## Problem

When the T3 server restarts or shuts down while a turn is running, recovery cancels the run, but the thread doesn't say why. Recovery builds the reason ("Cancelled because the server restarted before the provider work completed.") and passes it only to effect cleanup. In the timeline the run looks the same as a provider cancel or a user Stop.

To reproduce on main dd14848153 with a real server and a Claude turn: start a turn that runs a long foreground command. SIGKILL the server and start it again, or SIGTERM it. The run ends `cancelled`, and none of its items gives a reason. With "continue after server update" on, the next run starts with "T3 Code restarted and resumed this turn", but the cancelled run still says nothing.

## Change

When `ProviderRuntimeRecoveryService` cancels a run, it now adds one completed `system_notice` turn item to that run in the same commit. The title is "Server restarted" (startup) or "Server shut down" (shutdown), and the message is the reason recovery already builds. Web, mobile and MCP thread reads already render `system_notice`, so clients don't change.

- The item id comes from `ids.derive.runSignalTurnItem` (`signal: "server-recovery"`). Replaying recovery updates the same item; it never adds a second one.
- EventSink places the item after the run's existing items.
- Queued runs that recovery cancels never started provider work, so they get no notice.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#27048

Triaged via the automate [...]

A `preparing` run is included in runtime recovery, but this guard skips only `queued` runs. If the server stops before a `preparing` run starts, the new notice says provider work was interrupted when no provider work occurred. Use the existing `neverStarted(run)` condition to exclude that case. body:
## Problem

Cursor adds a `Co-authored-by: Cursor ` trailer to commits made through T3 even when `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` on the server sets `attribution.attributeCommitsToAgent` and `attributePRsToAgent` to `false`. `@cursor/sdk` builds the request context from an `attributionConfigProvider` and defaults to attributing when there is none, but its local runtime never supplies one and never reads `cli-config.json`. title: fix(opencode): a context overflow that OpenCode compacts no longer fails the turn
author: juliusmarminge
head: f07c9c6543a93b019ac10195b5fb99b459fbfac5
body:
## Problem

When an OpenCode 1.x provider request exceeds the model's context window, OpenCode publishes `session.error` with `ContextOverflowError`, stays busy, auto-compacts and keeps working. T3 ended the turn as `failed` on that first error, so a delegated task reported a failure to its parent while the OpenCode session went on editing the worktree with nobody watching it.

Reproduced against a real `opencode serve` 1.18.18 and a fake OpenAI-compatible model that answers one request with the reporter's `context_length_exceeded` error: OpenCode emits `session.error ContextOverflowError` → compaction summary → `session.compacted` → another agent step → idle. T3's adapter finalized the turn at the first event.

## Change

In the OpenCode 1.x adapter, a `ContextOverflowError` for a session with an active turn no longer finalizes that turn. The adapter keeps the failure on the turn, and `session.compacted` clears it. When the session goes idle, the turn completes normally if compaction succeeded. If compaction is off or itself overflowed, the turn fails with the same provider failure as before. Interrupts and broken event streams keep their existing outcomes. Every other `session.error` is unchanged. The OpenCode 2 adapter is not touched.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#26674

Triaged via the automated issue flow; GitCafe issue https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/26674.

title: fix(server): timed-out git commands that ignore SIGTERM no longer stall other git work
author: juliusmarminge
head: e2eb2435a84dc3b53e20a0ad17917934050c0fe4
body:
## Problem

A worktree launch for a branch already checked out in the project root stayed on "Preparing workspace" for about 7 hours. It then reported `git worktree add failed (branch_already_exists)`, an error git returns at once. Git commands with a timeout of 30 s or less share 8 process permits. When such a command timed out, the server sent its process group SIGTERM and then waited for it to exit with no limit, because git was spawned without `forceKillAfter`. A git process that does not exit on SIGTERM kept its permit until it exited on its own, and every later git call, including worktree creation, queued behind it.

Reproduced on main with the real git driver. Eight git commands with a 1 s timeout run a shell alias that ignores SIGTERM. Each ran until its `sleep` finished (8 s) and held its permit throughout. A `createWorktree` for an already checked-out branch, which fails in 57 ms on its own, waited 7.8 s and then failed with the same `branch_already_exists`.

## Change

Every git spawn in `GitVcsDriverCore` now uses `forceKillAfter: "1 second"`. A timed-out or interrupted command gets SIGTERM first, so git can remove its lock files. If it is still running 1 s later, it gets SIGKILL and its permit is released. The background status fetch already used this 1 s escalation through `forceKillAfterMs: 1_000`. That was the option's only caller, so the option is removed. Commands that exit normally never reach this cleanup.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#26 [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Synchronize the timeout with fixture startup.**

On a loaded host, the 200 ms timeout can expire before the shell installs the `SIGTERM` trap. The test can then pass without exercising force-kill, including on main. Emit a ready signal after installing the trap and trigger the timeout only after receiving it.

As per path instructions, logic bug tests must “fail on main for the relevant reason.”

_Source: Path instructions_

✅ Addressed in commit 3c6d27f

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Do not use a fixed sleep as the interruption window.**

After `trapped` is signaled, the test can be delayed for three seconds before `Fiber.interrupt(command)` runs. The fixture can then create `markerPath`, causing a false failure even when interruption terminates the process correctly. Keep the fixture alive until interruption and use `Fiber.interrupt(command)` as the completion point instead of relying on the sleep deadline.

title: fix(server): storage cleanup skips stale worktree paths under a regular file

head: d66f0d1b637b3b973a7a3c185144352ae290bcbe
body:
## Problem

Storage cleanup reports a thread as `failed` on every pass when its stored worktree path sits below something that is now a regular file. `fs.exists` maps only ENOENT to `false`. `access()` on a path under a file fails with ENOTDIR, which Effect maps to `BadResource`, so the error propagates and the entry becomes `BadResource: FileSystem.access ()`. The reporter had 467 of these stale legacy paths filling the report. A missing path (ENOENT) is already skipped quietly.

Reproduced on main 30eb7e7bb1 with the real server (`bin.ts serve` on a fresh base dir, `worktreeAfterDays: 30`). One thread's stored `worktreePath` was `/legacy-root/stored-workspace`, where `legacy-root` is a file, and a control thread's was `/missing-root/stored-workspace`. `server.runStorageCleanup` returned `failed: 1` for the ENOTDIR thread and nothing for the ENOENT one, for both archived and unarchived threads.

## Change

The worktree pass's first existence check now treats a `PlatformError` whose `cause.code` is `ENOTDIR` as "does not exist". It reuses the `catchIf` errno pattern this file already uses for `EINVAL`. Nothing can exist below a regular file, so the candidate is skipped like a missing path. Every other error, including other `BadResource` causes and `EACCES`, still fails as before. No thread data or history is changed.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#26585

- New test `storage cleanup reports and local file policies > skips a stored worktree pat [...]

title: fix(server): storage cleanup keeps worktrees whose file listing exceeds the inspection limit
author: juliusmarminge
head: d78822eca5017ee3817b963b472a47ccd63efbc5
body:
## Problem

Storage cleanup marks a worktree FAILED with `git: Git output exceeded 65536 bytes and was truncated.` when its `git status` listing, or its ignored-files listing under "Any local files", is larger than 64 KiB. It should keep the worktree with the reason "Local changes exceed the inspection limit". On main, a worktree with 3000 untracked files (`git status` exits 0 and prints 145,893 bytes) comes back `outcome: "failed"` under both `any-local-files` and `uncommitted-changes`. 3000 ignored `.env` entries do the same under `any-local-files`. Nothing was deleted, but the report shows a failure instead of the intended refusal.

## Change

`localChangesReason` already checks `stdoutTruncated`, but its two `git.execute` calls did not opt into bounded output. With the executor's default (`appendTruncationMarker: false`), the collector throws on overflow before that check can run. Both calls now pass `appendTruncationMarker: true`, so oversized output comes back truncated, and the existing guards return the KEEP reasons before any output is parsed. The shared executor's defaults are unchanged.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#26584

## Verification

- `vp test run src/storageCleanup.test.ts` (apps/server) adds three `it.live.each` cases, using the real cleanup service and real git:
  - "keeps a worktree under any-local-files when its untracked file listing exceeds the inspection limit"
  - the same under uncommitted-changes
  - "keeps a worktree under any-lo [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

**Keep the worktree when status stderr is truncated.**

Git can skip unreadable untracked directories and exit successfully. If enough warnings exceed 64 KiB, the incomplete status listing can look clean and cleanup can proceed.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Keep the worktree when ignored-file stderr is truncated.**

If Git cannot list enough ignored directories containing indexed paths, it can truncate stderr while omitting their files from stdout. Cleanup can then attempt removal under `any-local-files` instead of keeping the worktree.

author: juliusmarminge
head: dab7c4c3be60ca0d05887a52fd67ea85e32ac3f0
body:
## Problem

On mobile, an Un-settle pressed on a thread while its Settle is still waiting for the server did nothing: no haptic, no alert, and no command sent. This happens when the server stops responding without closing the connection, which leaves the Settle pending for about 15 s. When the Settle then failed and rolled back, the thread returned to the list, which looks as if the Un-settle had worked even though the server never received it.

Reproduction on `main` (`125b61954d`), using the Expo iOS dev client on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator paired to a dev server, with the server's port blocked by an iptables `DROP` (no reset):

1. Long-press a finished thread, then Settle. The thread moves to Settled and the Settle stays pending.
2. 3.6 s later, long-press the same thread in Settled, then Un-settle. Nothing happens and the thread stays Settled.
3. At about 15 s, "Could not settle thread: SocketReadError" appears and the thread goes back to the list. No unsettle command was ever sent.

## Change

`useThreadActionExecutor` dropped any action on a thread that already had a pending action. It now drops only a repeat of the latest pending action on that thread, so a double tap is still ignored. A different action now runs. Thread commands already go through one serial queue per thread, so it runs after the pending action and reports its own failure through the existing alert. This also covers changing your mind twice: Settle, then Un-settle, then Settle again all reach the queu [...]

An unconditional cleanup could remove the later action’s marker and allow a duplicate. Extend this test to finish the first action, then repeat the still-pending action.

title: fix(provider-acp-registry): prepared binary agents stay ready when the registry advances
author: juliusmarminge
head: ed562dd324cc6f2b9876577827aa091f4e4b3c4b
body:
## Problem

An ACP Registry agent installed as a binary (for example `devin`) stops working once the registry publishes a new version. The status check looks for the executable only under the registry's newest version, so an agent that is installed and working reports "ACP Registry agent 'devin' has not been prepared on this environment." It is then greyed out in the model picker, and threads can't start.

Reproduced on main @ 5211acf with a fresh dev server:
1. Settings → Providers → Add provider → ACP Registry → Devin. It installs 3000.11.228 and shows "Available".
2. Change Devin's `version` in the cached registry index to 3000.11.240, the same as a later registry refresh would, then restart the server.
3. The card reads "Not found · ACP Registry agent 'devin' has not been prepared…", and Devin can't be selected in a new thread's model picker. `tools/devin/3000.11.228/…/bin/devin` is still on disk.

## Change

In the binary branch of `inspect()`, an agent still counts as prepared when the current version's executable is missing but some version is already installed for a compatible platform target under `tools//`. `resolve()` already installs and launches the current registry version on demand, so binary agents now upgrade the same way npx/uvx agents already do.

Unchanged:
- An agent that was never installed still reports `unprepared`, and so does one whose binaries were uninstalled.
- When the current version is installed, its executable is still validated as before.

No [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Use a host-independent path assertion.**

When this test runs on Windows, `NodeServices.layer` supplies host-native path behavior. The current `/tools/...` assertion can fail despite a successful install. Build the expected fragment with `Path.Path`, or compare normalized path components.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Check an installed executable, not only its directory.**

If a user removes an older version’s executable but leaves its platform directory, this check returns `true`. `inspect()` then reports `ready` even though no binary is installed; `resolve()` must download a replacement and can fail. Record and validate the executable path for each completed install before treating that version as prepared.

title: fix(web): Ctrl + "+" zooms on keyboard layouts with a dedicated plus key
author: juliusmarminge
head: c9cfa24e263cef17d9f53ce2c94ef69767d70552
body:
## Problem

On keyboard layouts with a dedicated `+` key (German, Spanish, Italian at the US `]` position; Nordic at `-`; Portuguese at `[`), Ctrl/Cmd + `+` does not zoom the app. The shortcut matcher maps that key to the US key at the same physical position, so on a German layout Ctrl + `+` matches the default `mod+]` (go forward), the app calls `preventDefault`, and Electron's zoom accelerator never runs. On Linux there is no visible menu bar, so View → Zoom In is not available either.

Reproduced on main 07f7f97609 in the Electron desktop app under Xvfb with `setxkbmap -layout de` and real X key events: Ctrl + `+` produced `{key: "+", code: "BracketRight"}`, was `defaultPrevented`, navigated `#/welcome` → `#/settings/general`, and the zoom stayed at 1.

## Change

`shortcutKeyFromEvent` in `packages/shared/src/keybindings.ts` now keeps an unshifted, non-Alt `+` as `+` instead of replacing it with its physical key, the same way it already treats letters. Three cases keep physical matching, because existing bindings rely on it:

- **Shift:** US Ctrl+Shift+`=` still matches `mod+shift+=`.
- **Alt:** a German `alt+]` binding still matches.
- **Number row:** Czech and Slovak type `+` on `Digit1`, so Ctrl+1 still reaches `mod+1`.

The HTML-render frame bootstrap in `packages/shared/src/htmlRender.ts` has its own inline copy of the matcher. It gets the same rule, so the frame does not forward a chord the host then rejects.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#26383

##  [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Keep the physical `p` alias for unshifted `+` in the guest matcher.**

The guest matcher now sends an unshifted `+` with a non-`Digit` code through a branch that returns only `[l]`. On a layout where the KeyP position types `+`, `Ctrl+` no longer matches a `p` shortcut such as `mod+p`. The guest does not forward the event, but the app still resolves it as `mod+p`.

Keep the letter alias in that branch. Keep the code alias dropped, so the dedicated-plus fix still holds.

title: fix(pi): rewinding works after the Pi session was released
author: juliusmarminge
head: ac86d38d4e2d7fdc76922fce7eefd6fe7f56a925
body:
## Problem

Rewinding a Pi conversation fails with "The provider could not roll back this conversation" whenever its Pi runtime was released first (server restart, idle release, crash), and the automatic retries fail the same way. Checkpoint rollback opens a fresh Pi runtime and calls `rollbackThread` on it directly. A fresh Pi runtime has no registered thread, so `rollbackThread` stops at `Pi session has no registered thread` before any Pi RPC.

Reproduced on main (afc233492d) in the web dev server with Pi 1.4.0: two Pi turns, restart the server, then "Edit from here → Revert and keep changes" on the second message. With the same steps and no restart, the rewind succeeds.

## Change

When `PiAdapter.rollbackThread` runs on a runtime with no registered thread and the provider thread has a persisted native session, it loads that session through the adapter's existing `registerThread` path (`switch_session` to the session file), then forks as before. The Codex adapter already handles this by resuming its thread inside its own `rollbackThread`. The registration does not publish `provider_thread.updated`, because the rollback service persists the snapshot that `rollbackThread` returns. A thread with no native session still fails with the existing error.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#26312

## Verification

- New test `rolls back a persisted thread on a fresh runtime after its session was released` (`packages/provider-pi/src/server/adapter.test.ts`). It fails on m [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win**

**Require a native session ID before registration.**

If `nativeThreadRef` exists but `nativeId` is null, this guard calls `registerThread` without a session to resume. The provider reference schema permits that value. On a fresh runtime, registration can bind the persisted thread to Pi’s current session. If `piForkBoundary` returns `"nothing"`, rollback returns that session in the snapshot instead of failing with the existing “no registered thread” error. Check `nativeThreadRef?.nativeId != null` before registration. title: fix(server): failed provider updates show the updater's error, not its closing hint
author: juliusmarminge
head: 7d52c5f884f501297fd57b1ebd2f91de89cb02f4
body:
## Problem

When a provider update fails, the server builds the failure message from the last line of the updater's stderr. `claude update` prints its error first and a generic hint last, so a failed Claude update reads `Update command exited with code 1: Try running "claude doctor" for diagnostics` and leaves out the actual reason. Reproduced on main with a real native Claude Code 2.1.310 whose release host was unreachable: stderr was `Error: Failed to install native update` / `TelemetrySafeError: Failed to fetch version from https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/latest after 3 attempt(s): connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9` / `Try running "claude doctor" for diagnostics`, and the settings popover showed the doctor hint. The npm-installed Claude has the same problem: its failure output ends in `• Check if you need to login: npm whoami`.

## Change

`failureReason` in `providerMaintenanceRunner.ts` now picks the last output line that mentions an error or failure (`/error|fail/i`, stderr before stdout). If no line matches, it falls back to the last non-empty line, which was the old rule. For native Claude it picks the `TelemetrySafeError … 403 / ECONNREFUSED` line, for npm Claude `Failed to check for updates`, and Codex's single `Error: …` line still wins. The timeout message, the empty-output message and the full `output` are unchanged.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#26280

title: fix(server): slow title generations no longer hold every effect worker
author: juliusmarminge
head: fb471f6d0aac32e6e96b44dd98564fd57eb089b2
body:
## Problem

After a restart, threads with active turns stayed on "Working" for about 9 minutes with no provider process (https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/25962). The effect daemon has 4 workers shared by every effect type. A title generation can run for up to about 546 s (180 s CLI timeout × 3 tries), and restart recovery requeues title generations. Five of them took all four workers, so the threads' `provider-turn.start` effects were not claimed until a title finished.

Reproduced on main with a dev server: the text-generation CLI was a stand-in whose `exec` never returns. Titles were regenerated on four threads, then a follow-up was sent. All four workers were running titles, and the follow-up's `provider-turn.start` was still `pending` 20 s later, with the thread `starting` and no reply.

## Change

The daemon now runs at most `concurrency - 1` title generations at a time (3 of the default 4 workers). Every other effect type always has a worker. The cap is part of the shared claim predicate in `EffectOutbox.ts`, so `claimNext` and `nextClaimableAt` both apply it. A title held back by the cap neither gets claimed nor reports a past deadline, so idle workers sleep until a running title settles and wakes them. The count runs inside the atomic claim `UPDATE`, so concurrent workers cannot exceed the cap. With one worker there is no cap, as before. `drain`, `runRecoveryOnce` and direct `runOnce()` callers keep today's uncapped behaviour.

Fixes pin [...]

title: fix(server): Codex turns that auto-compact end instead of looping on restored context
author: juliusmarminge
head: 29a20b5f64240c8759032e249d4b505e141e69f1
body:
## Problem

When Codex auto-compacts in the middle of a turn, the Codex adapter re-injects the turn's `additionalContext` with `thread/inject_items` right away, while that turn is still running. Codex queues items injected into an active turn as that turn's pending input, and pending input makes the turn sample again. On a tight compaction limit, that extra sample compacts again, T3 injects again, and the turn never ends. Its run never goes terminal, so a delegated child keeps compacting after its final answer and the parent waits forever.

Reproduced on main against a real `codex app-server` (codex-cli 0.163.0), driven the way the adapter drives it, with a mock Responses endpoint that adds 0.5 s of model latency and an auto-compact limit just under the request size. When the inject is sent 50 ms after the compaction item, `turn/completed` never arrives: 37 compactions and 74 repeated final answers in 40 s. The same turn without the inject completes after one compaction. When the inject is sent immediately, the turn still ends, but only after an extra sampling round, an extra compaction and a duplicate final answer.

## Change

On a `contextCompaction` item completion, the adapter now records the native thread as needing its context restored and sends nothing. When that thread's `turn/completed` arrives, whatever its status, the adapter forks the existing `restoreAdditionalContext`. At that point Codex has no active turn for the thread, so it writes the items straight into hi [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Heavy lift**

**Serialize restoration before automatic goal continuation.**

After compaction, `turn/completed` forks `restoreAdditionalContext` without waiting for `thread/inject_items`. An active goal then creates a hold, and the next `turn/started` consumes that hold and registers a new native turn. If that notification arrives before injection completes, the restore request can run during the new turn and reintroduce the compaction loop. Coordinate restoration with the continuation boundary without blocking the notification reader. Add a regression case that combines compaction with an immediate goal continuation.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Wait until the replay driver receives the restoration request.**

`restoreRequested` resolves before `client.request`. The test can exit its scope before the replay driver checks the outbound frame, so it can miss an incorrect request. Signal the test from the `"restored"` inbound milestone instead.

title: fix(server): runtime prune no longer keeps a version whose directory is on the service PATH
author: juliusmarminge
head: 8c13bb6d1732b33e8f8c26df654435fc9857c910
body:
## Problem

On macOS the launch agent's `PATH` includes the running runtime's directory, `~/.t3/runtime/versions/`. The startup prune's `shellLauncherTargets` looks for `t3` in every `PATH` directory, so it finds that runtime's own entry binary `versions//t3`. It then appends the entry to the append-only `runtime/launchers`, and every later prune treats `` as referenced. Every version that reaches the service `PATH` is kept for good, about 270 MB each.

Reproduced on Linux with the real `prunePinnedRuntimes` (real filesystem and `/proc` scan) against a synthetic T3 home. Two service startups, on 0.1.0 and then 0.1.2, each with their own version directory on `PATH`. On main, `runtime/launchers` gains `versions/0.1.0/t3` and `versions/0.1.2/t3`, and 0.1.0 survives the prune after the update.

## Change

`shellLauncherTargets` now skips a candidate written as `versions//t3` that is not itself a link. That is a runtime's own entry binary, which the macOS service's `PATH` exposes. A launcher still pins the runtime it reaches: a link from elsewhere (`~/.local/bin/t3`, or a custom bin directory even under `versions/`), or a `PATH` directory that is itself linked to a version directory. The same check applies to entries already in `runtime/launchers`, so installs pinned by an earlier prune are released on the next prune without rewriting the file.

title: fix(server): PR sync and run-status checks stop reading whole thread histories
author: juliusmarminge
head: 124a42020d76da1b8bb3944100d35c7f2cced254
body:
## Problem

On large databases, two background reads hold the server's single SQLite reader far longer than they need to, so every other read, thread switches included, queues behind them (https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/24895: `thread.visit` median 12 s on a 22 GB database).

- The PR-sync sweep runs every minute. It builds full thread shells, which means reading every active thread's runs, turn items, provider threads and messages, even though it uses only thread payload fields.
- During a run start, the run-status checks (`isCurrentAttemptInStatus`, `shouldFinalizeRun`) each load the thread's whole runtime recovery projection to check a single run's status. That happens four to six times per run.

Reproduced on main (becf853def) with the red tests below:
- The sweep reads `runs`, `turn_items`, `provider_threads` and `messages`.
- A run start plus its two controls loads the recovery projection 6 times.

## Change

- `ProjectionStore.getPullRequestSyncSnapshot` reads only the thread payloads and the snapshot sequence, in one read transaction on the reader:
  - It filters archived threads on the maintained `archived_at` column.
  - It keeps the shell read's `unsettledOnly` condition and ordering.
  - It shares the shell's `MAX(sequence)` statement, so the existing sequence guard on `thread.pull-request.sync` behaves the same.
- `ThreadPullRequestServiceV2` uses this read for both the sweep and the single-thread refresh. The single-thread refresh previously made two s [...]

## Problem

## Change

- Red test at [c6ad88e92b](https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/commit/c6ad88e92b): expected recovery command was absent. After the fix, all 23 SSH tests in four files pass, including error propagation, preservation of stderr, no password prompt for a host-key failure, quoting, and option-shaped aliases.

threads.body:
**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Use terminal-specific quoting in the recovery command.**

When a Windows user copies a command containing an apostrophe into PowerShell, `shellSingleQuote` produces POSIX escaping such as `'o'\''brien@host'`. PowerShell requires doubled apostrophes instead. `cmd.exe` also does not use single quotes to group arguments. Keep POSIX quoting for the remote scripts in `tunnel.ts`, but format the recovery command for a named terminal shell. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_quoting_rules?view=powershell-7.5&utm_source=openai))

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Give changed host keys a separate recovery step.**

When the saved host key conflicts with the server key, running the suggested `ssh` command does not resolve the conflict. SSH continues to reject the saved key, so “then try again” does not complete the recovery. Distinguish this diagnostic from an unknown key. Tell the user to confirm the new fingerprint through a trusted source *before* replacing the conflicting known-hosts entry. Do not remove the entry automatically. ([man.openbsd.org](https://man.openbsd.org/man1/ssh-keygen.1?utm_source=openai))

   

Also applies to: 174-174

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Use an unqualified known-hosts entry for port 22.**

If the user selects port `22`, OpenSSH looks up `127.0.0.1`, not `[127.0.0.1]:22`. This entry cannot reproduce the changed-key case on that supported port, even after the configuration path is fixed. Write `127.0.0.1` for port `22` and retain the bracketed form for other ports. ([github.com](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/master/misc.c?utm_source=openai))

🟡 **Medium** `src/command.ts:159`

On Windows, the recovery command changes host specs containing `$` when pasted into PowerShell, so `ssh` receives a different host than the configured alias (for example, `me@dev$blue` becomes subject to `$blue` variable expansion). `terminalArg` wraps the value in double quotes, where PowerShell still expands variables; generate quoting for an explicitly identified shell that preserves literal `$` characters.

** Minor** · **Security & Privacy** · **Quick win**

**Escape double quotes and shell metacharacters in the Windows branch of `terminalArg`.**

On `win32`, `terminalArg` wraps the value in double quotes and does not escape anything inside. Aliases and usernames can contain `"`, `$`, or backtick. The copied recovery command can then break or run unexpectedly in PowerShell. In PowerShell, `$` and backtick expand inside double quotes. A hostile alias from a shared SSH config could inject a command when the user pastes the guidance.

Escape embedded `"` for the target shell. You can also add a Windows-specific check that refuses to print a command for unsafe values, and show only the host spec instead.

The current tests expect double quotes on `win32`, so update the test expectation if you pick a different form. cmd.exe does not group arguments with single quotes, so choose a target shell and document the choice.

title: fix(server): a Claude thread waiting on a ScheduleWakeup stays in Working

head: 88635e016a1054e19225994b27b0448979792e8b
body:
## Problem

When a Claude agent calls Claude Code's native `ScheduleWakeup` tool (for example in a self-paced `/loop`) and ends its turn, the thread leaves Working and lands in the inbox as if it were done, although Claude will start a new turn on its own when the delay ends. Repro on main ([ed3f965e07](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/commit/ed3f965e07)): Working section on, new Claude Sonnet 5.5 thread, ask it to call `ScheduleWakeup` with `delaySeconds: 120`. The turn completes with `pendingBackgroundTasks: []`, the thread moves to the inbox, and about two minutes later Claude starts the wake turn by itself.

## Change

The Claude adapter now records a pending wakeup from the `ScheduleWakeup` tool result (`tool_use_result.scheduledFor`). While it is pending, the provider thread publishes one extra `background_task` entry, "Scheduled wakeup", in `pendingBackgroundTasks`. Existing paths already treat that entry as waiting work: the thread stays in Working as "Waiting", the background-work banner shows it with Stop, auto-settle waits, and the idle session release keeps the Claude process alive (a wakeup can be up to an hour out, past the 30-minute idle timeout).

The record lives outside the adapter's background-task roster, so a pending wakeup does not refuse a model, mode or provider change. Such a change replaces the Claude process, which cancels the wakeup and clears the record.

The record clears when:
- the wakeup is cancelled (`stop: true`, which returns `scheduledF [...]

threads.body:
**🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Do not apply the early-fire margin to a task-notification wake.**

`handleSdkMessageFrame` tracks `system/init` before routing it. When the session is idle, a `task_notification` is already buffered before the notification continuation starts. Therefore, an init within 120 seconds of `scheduledFor` can run with `activeTurn === null` and delete the scheduled wakeup record.

That deletion makes `hasPendingBackgroundWork` return `false`, so the process can be released before the scheduled reply.

title: fix(server): branch switch no longer kills a slow git checkout
author: juliusmarminge

body:
## Problem

Switching branches in a large repository can take longer than 10 seconds. The branch picker killed `git checkout` at that deadline, leaving HEAD on the old branch while some files already contained target-branch content. Reproduced through the real web client with a required 15-second Git smudge filter.

## Change

Run branch-switch checkout without a timeout, following the existing long-running Git command behavior. Keep checkout serialization, scoped subprocess cleanup, ref validation and error diagnostics.

## Scope and approval

Fixes https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/22245
GitCafe: https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/22245
Triaged bug via the automated issue flow. This fixes the existing branch-switch operation without adding settings or changing contracts.

## Verification

- Added a regression test before the fix: a controlled real checkout with the test clock advanced 60 seconds failed with `Git command timed out`. The same test passes with the fix.
- `vp test run src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.test.ts` from `apps/server`: 162 passed.
- Focused lead rerun for slow checkout and missing-ref diagnostics: 6 passed.
- Scoped lint: no errors; one existing warning outside the change. Server typecheck: passed.
- Both independent reviewers returned MERGE. No changed rendering paths; [visual matrix](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/4611c8d4124130da/empty-visual-matrix.md) is empty (0/0).

| Real runtime proof | Before | Aft [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Heavy lift**

**Narrow the shared-config lock around remote checkouts.**

`execute` holds the per-`gitCommonDir` semaphore for the full checkout because `switchRef` sets `writesSharedConfig` for every remote ref. This remains true when `localTrackingBranch` already exists and the checkout only switches to that branch.

The previous 10-second timeout bounded this hold. With `timeoutMs: null`, a checkout that remains pending can block shared-config operations in other linked worktrees until interruption or process exit. This includes branch operations that update shared configuration, but not every branch operation.

Preserve serialization for actual shared-config writes. Avoid holding the semaphore for the long checkout itself. Reuse the existing tracking branch without `writesSharedConfig`; for a remote ref without one, separate the long checkout from the serialized upstream-configuration write only if the resulting branch-selection behavior remains unchanged.

title: fix(server): update branch labels after terminal checkouts
author: juliusmarminge
head: 99c17e1999ce4556efbc17093f716150d9652223
body:
## Problem

Creating or switching branches in the integrated terminal leaves the session composer and Thread details branch labels stale until the window regains focus. Reproduced with the real web dev server on Linux using an isolated Git repository and stopped threads.

## Change

Watch each subscribed checkout’s HEAD directory, including linked worktrees, and refresh status when Git replaces HEAD. Share the watch between subscribers and release it after the last subscriber leaves. Retry failed checkout refreshes with backoff capped at 30 seconds, and restart a completed watcher when a later subscriber joins while preserving existing owners. Publish the checked-out branch with its corresponding PR and upstream metadata, retrying reads interrupted by a checkout. Background status polling also refreshes local branch state. A failed local read leaves remote counts uncached so the next poll retries local status. Read canonical branch names so a same-named tag cannot prevent the refresh.

## Scope and approval

Fixes https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/7409

Triaged bug via the automated issue flow: [#7409](https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/7409). Synthetic fixture data and its seed script are included as required by the triage evidence procedure. No client contract or provider protocol changes.

## Verification

- Red proof on the before revision: the original external-checkout regression fails with `expected [] to deeply equal ['repro']`. [Failure transcript](https [...]

threads.body:
🟠 **High** `vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:535`

When `localStatus` fails for the displayed branch, this fallback caches the new remote counts without refreshing the cached local status. Later polls see `branchShown && !countsMoved` and skip the local read, so local totals can remain stale even after the transient error clears. Preserve a pending local refresh or otherwise retry the read after this fallback.

No longer relevant as of 2a04d5e1cabf9c9f9af28f06b460b8422e6932aa

**🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Scrub inherited Git repository state before invoking Git.**

If the caller sets `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, or `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, the inherited environment can redirect the helper's `git -C` commands. This can make `init`, `add`, or `commit` use the caller's repository or index instead of the fixture. The script is a manually run fixture generator, so this is a narrow minor-risk issue, not a major production-impact issue.

✅ Addressed in commit 2c458fd

🟠 **High** `vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:788`

A checkout handled while `index.lock` exists leaves the branch label stale for `includeRemote: false` subscribers until another `HEAD` change or explicit refresh. The failed `refreshCheckedOutRef` is discarded by `Effect.ignoreCause`, and removing `index.lock` emits no event that passes the `HEAD` filter; retry transient refresh failures after a delay.

No longer relevant as of bd7fbe65f804f00d049ad6301b2bcdd27bb50087

**🔒 Security & Privacy** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Replace raw Cause logging with bounded diagnostics.**

`Effect.ignoreCause({ log: true })` logs the complete Cause from the HEAD refresh and watcher paths. That Cause can contain arbitrary failure or defect data. This violates the effect-services logging requirement.

Use `remoteRefreshFailureDiagnostics(cause)` at both sites. `Effect.catchCause` still consumes the failure, so the refresh stream and watcher lifecycle keep their current behavior.

✅ Addressed in commit 42eb1f0

title: fix(web): collapsed reasoning previews no longer process the whole block
author: juliusmarminge
head: 8f71c2a691eb83808a1269d60ffbbb7336abc0b3
body:
## Problem

Opening a thread with a large reasoning trace can freeze web and Electron desktop while rendering a collapsed label. The full Markdown was parsed, then `remarkThoughtPreview` repeatedly concatenated and normalized the growing text for every fragment, producing quadratic work. This addresses [#22985](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/22985), mirrored as [#22988](https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/22988).

## Change

Bound collapsed and live preview source parsing to 8,192 characters, and stop transformer traversal after 2,048 characters. Text fragments are joined and whitespace-normalized once per text run. The source lookahead lets ordinary links and inline formatting close before the output cap. Expanded reasoning keeps the complete original text; layout, classes, and expand/collapse behavior are unchanged.

## Scope and approval

Fixes #22985

Triaged bug via the automated issue flow; GitCafe mirror #22988.

## Verification

Finite lookahead can leave exceptionally long inline constructs or distant reference definitions unresolved, or consume the source budget on hidden markup. Very long formulas can be truncated. These limits affect compact labels; expanded content stays complete. Mobile uses a separate plain-text preview renderer.

Final-head, five-sample medians (Codex proof-audit run):

| 190k-character fixture / measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mixed Markdown, transformer only | 9,778.89 ms | 0.348 ms |
| Mixed Markdown, [...]

threads.body:
🟡 **Medium** `scripts/seed-reasoning-preview-fixtures.mjs:101`

When the selected template contains a web-sent message, this transaction rolls back and creates no fixtures because the cloned message and turn-item IDs collide with the original rows' primary keys. `swap` only changes the thread token and `native-*` IDs, but web message IDs and their derived turn-item IDs contain neither; remap those IDs and their references, or reject templates whose IDs cannot be rewritten.

**🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Resolve the canonical database path before enforcing the live-database guard.**

If the supplied `statev2.sqlite` path or a parent directory is a symlink into `~/.t3`, `NodePath.resolve()` keeps the alias path. The lexical prefix check can pass, while `new NodeSqlite.DatabaseSync(dbPath)` opens the live database. The script can then archive all currently unarchived threads and modify the database.

This script requires an explicit developer-supplied path, so the risk is limited to this workflow.

**🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Derive the reasoning position from stored turn-item positions.**

The issue is not that `assistant.ordinal` uses a different scheme. `EventSink` normalizes each turn-item payload to the position allocated by `TurnItemPositionStore`. When the user and assistant positions are consecutive, `assistant.ordinal - 1` equals the user’s position.

Because `orchestration_v2_turn_item_positions` has `UNIQUE (thread_id, ordinal)`, `INSERT OR REPLACE` removes the user’s position row before inserting the reasoning row. Derive a separate position from the stored user and assistant positions. If no gap exists, shift later positions before inserting the reasoning position.

🟡 **Medium** `scripts/seed-reasoning-preview-fixtures.mjs:175`

For a completed run containing only a user message and an assistant message, the reasoning fixture shares the user's ordinal, so it sorts before the prompt and `INSERT OR REPLACE` overwrites the user's position. Assign distinct ordered ordinals to the retained user, reasoning, and assistant items and update their positions accordingly.

title: fix(web): convert composer list markers completed later
author: juliusmarminge
head: 2f1053ae6ef0f80aa62461f184c02972c2ad16f4
body:
## Problem

Completing a list marker inside existing composer text left a paragraph on screen while saving list Markdown. Rebuilding the draft then changed its appearance. Reproduces [#22989](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/22989), mirrored as [#22997](https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/22997).

## Change

Choose option (a): make the editor match its Markdown, preserving the expected bullet and existing draft-rebuild behavior. A ProseMirror append transaction normalizes only changed, unindented top-level paragraphs. It mirrors existing bullet (`-`, `*`, `+`), ordered (`1.`, `1)`), and dash-task markers, preserves marker spelling and formatting, and groups conversion with the edit for undo. Styled literal markers, code, existing list items, and blockquotes are excluded. Composition waits for the next non-composition transaction.

## Scope and approval

Fixes https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/22989

Triaged bug via the automated issue flow; GitCafe mirror https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/22997.

## Verification

> Superseded: the evidence in this section (head 9c3c3acbc6) is replaced by **Evidence** below, captured on the merged head.

Evidence re-captured as narrated before/after recordings per EVIDENCE.md (merge-base [680152e27b](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/commit/680152e27b2a961686389ca69a1557cbb2c55f08) vs head [9c3c3acbc6](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/commit/9c3c3acbc65b6cd756052c03ce9a41a905e40b90)). 58 of 70 matrix rows re [...]

threads.body:
**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Flush pending normalization when composition ends without a state transaction.**

`listNormalizationPlugin` retains positions for composition-tagged transactions, but it only processes them during a later `appendTransaction` call. ProseMirror can finish composition without dispatching a transaction when the DOM and selection are already synchronized. In that case, the pending paragraph remains literal after composition ends.

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Join compatible adjacent lists after wrapping.**

`tr.wrap` creates a new list around the paragraph, but this path does not merge it with an adjacent compatible list. The serializer emits adjacent list nodes as consecutive Markdown items, while `buildTiptapContent` groups items with the same `listKey`. The editor can therefore differ from the document rebuilt from its Markdown.

Join only when the list-grouping keys match. A node-type-only check would incorrectly merge lists that use different bullet markers, such as `-` and `*`.

🟡 **Medium** `evidence/drive-composer-list-markers.mjs:73`

When `--storage-state` contains an explicit appearance that differs from `--theme`, the capture uses the saved app theme, so `--theme light` can produce dark artifacts labeled `light`. The `colorScheme` setting only controls the browser preference, and `useTheme` honors the saved explicit mode; set or validate the app appearance before capturing.

🟡 **Medium** `src/composer-rich-text-doc.ts:646`

`Shift-Backspace` cannot undo a list input rule: `undoInputRule()` restores the literal prefix in a non-history transaction, and this normalizer immediately wraps it again. Exclude input-rule reversal transactions from normalization, not just history transactions.

No longer relevant as of 2f1053ae6ef0f80aa62461f184c02972c2ad16f4

🟠 **High** `src/composer-rich-text-doc.ts:682`

Editing the literal paragraph `* *` at its start to produce `* * *` wraps it as a bullet list, but `buildTiptapContent` restores the same Markdown as a horizontal rule, so the editor content changes after draft restoration. `parseListPrefix` accepts thematic-break syntax here without the horizontal-rule check used by `buildTiptapContent`; exclude horizontal-rule lines before wrapping them.

title: fix(desktop): wait for the local server to exit when quitting
author: juliusmarminge
head: 2556793610b8044edef366a6306e6e916f8af6b7
body:
## Problem

Quitting desktop could finish while its local backend still held the T3 home's single-writer lock. The five-second outer wait expired at the same deadline as SIGKILL escalation, leaving relaunch unable to start a server.

## Change

Wait for the existing scoped process teardown and exit acknowledgement even after the warning threshold. This preserves the spawner's SIGTERM → five-second grace → SIGKILL → final one-second wait, without adding another signal path. Normal quit and updater quit share a seven-second threshold: 7s > 5s grace + 1s kill wait. A concurrent unregister cannot propagate its cleanup interruption into sibling backend stops. Cooperative shutdown returns immediately. An OS-uninterruptible backend can keep quit waiting rather than leaving it alive and claiming shutdown completed.

## Scope and approval

Fixes #22983
GitCafe: https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/22983
Triaged bug via the automated issue flow.

Existing process coverage is unchanged: POSIX teardown signals the backend's process group; Windows uses taskkill /T /F while the leader is alive, not job objects. Descendants in separate groups/scopes depend on their server-side teardown; this does not claim to kill detached provider trees or the Linux side of WSL through a Windows process-group signal.

Validation:
- Fake-process baseline: 3 failed, 11 passed; stop and pool quit resolved with the backend still alive.
- Targeted manager/pool suites after the fix: 15 passed. Coverage inclu [...]

threads.body:
🟡 **Medium** `scripts/quit-lock-evidence.sh:158`

An unknown `FIXTURE` exits with status 2 but leaves the already-launched Electron main process, backend, and `headless-desktop` wrapper running, so they continue holding the isolated home’s lock. The rejection at line 186 happens after `launch primary`; validate the fixture before launching.

```diff
+case "$FIXTURE" in
+  F1|F2|F3|F4|F12) ;;
+  *) echo "unknown fixture $FIXTURE" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+esac
```

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Guard F2’s CDP endpoint before sending the close request.**

`CDP_PORT` defaults to shared port `9333`. If another process owns that port, `cdp_close` can send `window.close()` to its page because it does not compare the listener with `MAIN`. Use a run-specific port or fail unless the listener belongs to the launched Electron process.

The `CDP_PORT` environment override reduces the risk, but no automatic conflict or ownership check exists. This is a minor issue for a manual evidence script, not a major product issue.

**🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Fail F2 when the CDP close request fails.**

If CDP is unavailable, `cdp_close` can fail without closing the window. The script still enters `wait_main_exit`, which has no time limit, so F2 can hang indefinitely. Check the CDP result and stop the owned processes on failure. Treat a socket close or the three-second CDP timeout as a failure unless the close request was acknowledged.

**🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Validate the fixture before launching Electron.**

For an unknown fixture, the script reaches this exit only after it has launched Electron and the backend. This path skips `cleanup_orphans` and can leave the isolated home’s lock held. Reject unsupported fixtures before `launch primary`; also arrange run-owned cleanup for interrupted runs.

A freshly observed subscription snapshot can include a session reset timestamp that has already passed. Before: expiry 16:30 and the 16:45 timeline entry says “Open T3 to refresh” with no rows. After: session 100% remaining and weekly 70% remaining at 16:45, then both rows expire at 17:00. Changing only the session reset to 17:30 produces the same 17:00 deadline.

- `vp test run apps/mobile/src/widgets/subscriptionUsageSnapshot.test.ts`: 14 pass [...]

threads.body:
🟡 **Medium** `scripts/seed-widget-fixture-22973.mts:72`

Reapplying a fixture after editing either widget source overwrites those edits without warning. Because `fixtureModule` exists, the dirty-tree check is skipped and `revert()` checks out both files from `HEAD`; validate that the changes are only the generated patch or preserve user edits before reverting.

**📐 Maintainability & Code Quality** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Register the fixture script so Knip accepts it.**

CI reports this file as unused, so `vp run knip:check` fails. Register the command as a recognized entrypoint or add a narrow Knip exemption. Verify that the lint step passes.

_Source: Pipeline failures_

**🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Protect edits when reapplying the fixture.**

A dirty tracked-file state is expected after the first `apply()`. However, a later `apply()` calls `revert()`, which runs `git checkout HEAD -- ...tracked` and can discard edits made after the previous apply. Do not reject the script’s own dirty state. Instead, reset files only when they still match the script-generated patch; otherwise stop without overwriting edits.

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Validate the coordinator hook before changing files.**

If the hook text has changed, this check throws after `apply()` has restored the tracked files, generated the fixture module, and possibly replaced `subscriptionUsageSnapshot.ts` with the before-ref version. Move the hook check ahead of those writes so a failed apply leaves the working tree unchanged.

title: fix(server): agent continuations preserve the working timer start
author: juliusmarminge
head: 43c77ada7d2af22e23dcdbf8032b0d3987ca45fd
body:
## Problem

Agent messages queued behind active work started a new run without the original work timestamp, so the working timer reset during the same task. Reproduced with Codex GPT-6.1-Sol in an isolated client: the original run lasted 2m7s, then its queued agent continuation showed 21s. Addresses [#22931](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/22931).

Stamp the existing `workStartedAt` field when an agent continuation drains automatically. Immediate delegated-child updates keep the existing child-completion semantics. Fresh user and unrelated idle-agent requests, explicit Resume, and Send now start fresh clocks. No UI, subscriptions, or timer-cadence changes.

Fixes https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/22931

title: fix(server): worktrees cut from a non-default base no longer show the base's PR
author: t3dotgg
head: 8d6a704c1bcb3318dad07679ee1ec7fb432370a4
body:
A thread on a worktree cut from a non-default base such as `dev` showed the newest merged `dev -> main` release PR, even though the branch had no PR of its own. Every thread on such a checkout showed the same number, and the merged state could settle the thread.

The branch tracks `origin/dev`, so the PR lookup asked for `--head dev`. The existing guard only treated the default branch as a base. Now the lookup also treats the upstream as a base when it matches the branch's recorded `gh-merge-base`, which T3 writes when it creates a worktree from a base. The branch then looks up PRs under its own name, as it already does for a default-branch upstream. This covers the thread row and composer footer, since both read the same server status, and the branch PR lookup that shares the same cache. Cross-repository upstreams are not changed. A branch made with plain `git checkout -b feature/x origin/dev` and no recorded base is not changed: git gives no way to tell it apart from `git checkout --track remote/branch`, where a differently named upstream really is the PR head (an existing test covers that case).

title: fix(server): thread search finds phrases inside quotes and their comments
author: only21mil
head: f659f078e4411fd933a8f3620184e248523cec69
body:
## Problem

Thread search can't find a phrase inside a quote or its comment (https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/22304). A quote is stored in the message text as an `[Assistant quote](t3-citation://v1/…)` link, and `URLSearchParams` encodes the quote and comment inside it: `what are you talking about` is stored as `what+are+you+talking+about`. Thread search matches that stored text, both through the message index and the fallback scan, so phrases with spaces never match, and accented, CJK and apostrophe words in a quote never match through the index. Single words do, including words from the quote's hidden `prefix` and `suffix` selection context, so a thread can show up for a word its reader never saw in it.

## Change

- When `ProjectionStore` projects a message, it now stores `search_text` on `orchestration_v2_projection_messages`: `assistantCitationsToPlainText(text)`, the helper the queued-message and stash previews already use. A quote becomes its text plus `Comment: …`, without the link or its hidden context. The column is `NULL` when that equals the stored text, so plain messages aren't stored twice. Every `message.updated` upsert rewrites it, so edits keep it current.
- Migration 081 adds the column, recreates the message search triggers, and backfills existing history. The backfill pages through messages whose payload contains `t3-citation://`, 500 at a time by `message_id`, and writes `search_text` only where the readable text differs; the update trigger re-ind [...]

title: fix(server): a limited provider's queue stays held after another provider's turn succeeds
author: Marve10s
head: e0382359a34a8a6de2583e1687eff26a53b82130
body:
## Problem

A usage-limit failure holds a thread's queued messages only until any later run on the thread executes. When provider A hits its limit with A-selected messages still queued and the user then completes a turn on provider B, the queue starts on its own. Each queued A message runs against A's still-active limit, fails with `usageLimitExceeded`, is consumed, and flips the thread back to A. Reported in https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/21705 and reproduced twice there with native provider errors and run timestamps.

The gate in `usageLimitHoldsQueue` reads A's latest session error but passes every run on the thread to `usageLimitBlockedRun`, which looks only at the thread's latest executed run. After B's success that run is B's completed run, so the gate returns false even though A's own latest run is still the usage-limit failure.

## Change

`usageLimitHoldsQueue` now evaluates only the runs of the provider the queued message selects. When A's limited run is still the thread's latest run, the queue stays held as before.
