title: fix(web): full-screen HTML pages fit their content and zoom by reflowing
author: Zeus-Deus
head: 9f4a723e17ee804b899897a9649604878cafb85d
body:
## Problem

Opening an `html_render` page full screen made it hard to read. The page was written for the 728px reply column, but the dialog stretched it across 92vw (about 1700px on a typical display). Paragraphs became single long lines, and `vw`-sized type roughly doubled. The frame was always 86vh tall: a short page sat in an empty card, and a long one scrolled inside the iframe, where the injected CSS hides the scrollbar. Zoom used CSS `zoom`, which never changes the page's layout width. At 150% the page ran off the right and bottom edges with two nested scroll areas, and at 50% it shrank into a corner.

## Change

All changes are in `HtmlRenderDialog`:

- **Width:** the card is capped at `min(92vw, 1176px)`, a 1144px page plus padding. That's the widest width the server measures a page at, so a page stays close to the layout it was written for.
- **Height:** the frame takes the height the page already reports (`onContentHeight`). Before the first report, it falls back to the server-measured heights for that width. The card's old fixed height becomes its `max-height`, so short pages get a short card and tall ones scroll the card, never the iframe.
- **Zoom:** kept, but it now divides the page's layout width. At every zoom level the page reflows to fill the card instead of overflowing it or leaving empty space.

`HtmlRenderFrame` now passes its `HtmlRenderReference` to the dialog instead of just the title. Mobile uses its own WebView with native scrolling and isn't affecte [...]

The desktop converts every valid WSL UNC path with `wslUncPathToLinuxPath` without comparing its distro with the target. `parseWslUncPath(pickedPath)` then returns `null`, so the native clone branch submits that path using `addProjectCloneFlow.environmentId` for A. title: fix(web): don't save retention age until committed
author: macodev00
head: 85f953017c3207022f193a9978e3b651dda65308
body:
In Settings → Worktrees and Settings → Maintenance, switching an Off retention rule on used to save 8 days at once, and any saved age can start a cleanup sweep before the user picks the age they want. Now switching on opens a focused age draft showing 8 and saves nothing. Enter (including on the untouched 8) saves the shown age, and an edited or stepped age is saved when focus leaves the rule's row. On a rule with no saved age, stepper clicks and arrow keys only change the shown age, so raising it from 8 never saves a shorter age on the way. Escape, switching back off, or leaving an untouched draft discards it, and moving focus to the row's switch holds an edited age, so switching off with the mouse or keyboard saves nothing. Switching a saved rule off still saves null at once and hides its age right away; a failed save brings the age back, and a failed first save returns the rule to Off with the existing error toast. All four rules (inactive worktrees, settled worktrees, browser artifacts, rotated logs) share the control.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#14743

## Takeover
Taken over from @macodev00, whose PR found the bug, the shared `RetentionControl`, and the need for the save hook to report failure (`useScopedSettings` now returns `Promise`; its other callers ignore it).
`RetentionControl` was rebuilt from main's version: one state value tracks an open draft or the in-flight first save, and a `held` flag keeps an age that must not be saved yet (focus on the row's switch, or a ste [...]

threads.body:
🟠 **High** `settings/StorageSettings.tsx:216`

In a German locale, pressing Enter with `1.000` saves 1 day instead of 1000, so retention can delete artifacts far earlier than requested. `Number(raw)` interprets the localized display text as JavaScript numeric syntax; commit the numeric value already parsed by `NumberField` instead.

```suggestion
                if (draft !== null) commitDays(draft);
```

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Clear holding mode when the scoped save fails.**

When `value` is `null`, `commitDays` sets `"holding"` before calling `onChange`. A failed `serverEnvironment.updateSettings` call does not change the settings prop, and the error toast does not notify `RetentionControl`. Because an unchanged `null` does not trigger reconciliation, `enabled` remains true for the lifetime of the mounted control even though the persisted value is still `null`. Return the scoped save result and clear holding mode when that save fails while the prop remains `null`.

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Clear `pointerInsideRef` when the pointer leaves the control.**

For mouse pointers, a release outside the root does not reach its bubbling `onPointerUp` handler. The ref can remain `true`. Touch pointers can be implicitly captured, so `pointerup` may still reach the control; the original claim is not universal.

If an outside focus change blurs the draft before that `pointerup`, the stale ref makes `onBlur` skip `discardDraft()`. A document-level `pointerup` listener is not sufficient because pointer and focus event ordering is not guaranteed. Clear the ref on `onPointerLeave`; captured touch pointers still clear through `onPointerUp` or `onPointerCancel`.

✅ Addressed in commit 87649a2

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Move the `valueRef` write out of render.**

Line 129 writes a ref during render. The supplied CI logs show that this causes a React Compiler bailout and fails `reactCompilerCoverage.test.ts`. Synchronize the ref after a committed render, while preserving the check for a save result that resolves quickly. React also prohibits ref writes during render. ([react.dev](https://react.dev/reference/react/useRef?utm_source=openai))

As per coding guidelines, “Every file under `apps/web/src` must compile” and the compiler coverage test “fails on any skip.”

_Sources: Coding guidelines, Linters/SAST tools, Pipeline failures_

✅ Addressed in commit c72a309

**🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Reset drafts when the settings scope changes.**

`RetentionControl` only resets its draft when `value` changes. If two scopes have the same retention value, a draft remains active across the scope change. The updated `onChange` then targets the new scope, so committing the draft can save the previous scope's age to the new scope. Key the control by a stable scope identity or reset its local state when that identity changes.

✅ Addressed in commit 8fb4132

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Keep a new draft when a pending off save completes.**

If a user turns an enabled rule off and then turns it on before the off save completes, the switch opens a new draft. When the off save updates `value` to `null`, this reconciliation resets the mode to `"synced"` and clears the draft. The rule appears Off, and any age entered in the new draft is lost. Preserve the active draft when the arriving `null` belongs to the earlier off save.

✅ Addressed in commit 8fb4132

**📐 Maintainability & Code Quality** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Dispose the screen in `openDraft` if the click fails.**

`openDraft` renders and then clicks, but it returns a bare `screen`. If the `act` call or the click throws, nothing unmounts the screen. The container stays in `document.body` and leaks into later tests. The bare `await render(...)` can also trigger `t3code/require-disposable-render`.

Put the screen in an `AsyncDisposableStack` and `move()` it out only on success. The callers keep their `await using screen = await openDraft(...)`.

As per coding guidelines, "A helper that renders and then waits or clicks puts the screen in an `AsyncDisposableStack` and `move()`s it out only on success, so a failed wait still unmounts."

_Source: Coding guidelines_

✅ Addressed in commit 08a14c5

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Clean up generated harness files before repository checks.**

`prepare.mjs` leaves the generated files on disk. Running the fixture and then `vp typecheck` can fail because the harness uses `useState(null)` and later calls `setValue(v)`, assigns `window.proof` without a `Window` declaration, and returns `Promise` where `RetentionControl` requires `Promise | void`.

`.gitignore` rules prevent accidental staging, but they do not exclude the files from TypeScript or React Compiler coverage. Add teardown after the browser run, or generate the TSX outside `apps/web/src` and remove both files after the run. Keep ignore rules as an additional safeguard against staging.

✅ Addressed in commit 08a14c5

**🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Use `vi.waitFor` or `expect.element` for the DOM assertion.**

This direct `expect` reads the input before the browser-test synchronization boundary. Wrap the assertion in `await vi.waitFor(...)` or use `expect.element(...)` so the test observes the committed DOM state.

As per coding guidelines, browser tests must assert through `expect.element` or `vi.waitFor`.

_Source: Coding guidelines_

body:
`task_cancel` could stop a delegated child's background work after its turn completed while `task_status` still reported `completed` and the parent task stayed running. fixes https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/16739.

cancellation now commits `cancelledRunId` with the child's stop and interrupt outbox, then settles completed work as `interrupted`. it preserves published results, failures, and unrelated questions. parent and child locks exclude new delegation during cleanup; direct remote descendants dispatch under the held child lock, and terminal-task cancellation uses the same locking path.

verification: blacksmith `vp run check:changed` passed format, lint, knip, graphql, typechecks for 32 affected packages, and 136 tests across 10 files. the new remote-descendant case reproduced a lock hang before the fix and passes afterward. real codex and the web client verified a finished intermediate turn with a running nested `sleep 3600`: cancellation returned `interrupted / result_available`, retained `WAITING_FOR_BACKGROUND_CHILD`, and persisted its cancellation run id. cancelling an already-completed task preserved its completed status and published result; the cancelled task remained interrupted.

unverified: live remote environments, claude native background work, electron, mobile, and relay/tunnel connections. existing integration coverage exercises provider background work, refusal, follow-ups, checkpoint races, and restart recovery.

prior matching main/pr reproducti [...]

threads.body:
**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Record cancellation on follow-up runs and dismiss their settled questions.**

When `Stop` targets an active follow-up that is waiting on background work, this guard rejects it because the follow-up is not the original fork task and has a run with `delegatedTaskId === input.taskId`. The cancellation path therefore does not record `cancelRequestedAt`. Finalization can then keep the completed run as `completed` instead of converting it to `interrupted`, while retaining its interim result.

Changing only this guard is insufficient. The cleanup gate checks cancellation only on the original fork task, so it skips pending-question dismissal for the cancelled follow-up's settled run. Accept the follow-up while retaining the terminal-task check. Then associate cleanup with the cancelled task and settled result run. Keep the existing continuation-chain filter so unrelated runs remain pending.

This is a narrow functional-correctness issue. The correction is localized and has high value.

✅ Addressed in commit 016597c

**🩺 Stability & Availability** | ** Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Bound the child stop while holding the parent lock.**

`thread.stop` queues provider interruption without waiting for the provider. However, `cancelDelegatedTask` can wait for the child lock while holding the parent lock. `stopWorkflow` can hold that child lock for up to 15 seconds during `stopTask`, delaying parent dispatches and finalizers.

Apply the same bound to `input.stop`, or use a lock-phase protocol that preserves the cancellation marker before releasing the parent lock.

** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win**

**Preserve `cancelledTask` when the Stop plan is empty.**

`cancelDelegatedTask` creates and passes `cancelledTask` for an unsettled active task. `dispatchWithReceiptEffect` appends that marker only during `commitCommand`. If `thread.stop` produces no events or effects, the early receipt path returns before the commit, and the cancellation marker is lost.

✅ Addressed in commit 3188d3d

title: fix(server): new worktrees refresh their index once, so captures and status stop re-hashing every file
author: josephv123
head: 32e86fad359a205104bae1e1087db12bb3dd1872
body:
## Problem

A worktree T3 creates for a thread stays "racily clean" until something outside T3 rewrites its index, and until then every checkpoint capture and every status refresh in it re-reads the whole checkout (https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/21328).

`git worktree add` writes the files first and the index last. Git re-reads, on every status, diff and `add`, each file whose mtime falls in the index's own second or later. With the `checkout.workers=0` that `createWorktree` passes, a t3code checkout (28,271 files, 396 MB) finishes in about 0.63 s here, so often all of it lands in that second. Nothing T3 runs ever writes the index:
- status polling uses `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` and plumbing `diff-index` (https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/14718);
- captures work on a copy of the index;
- the agents don't either: Claude Code's startup commands use `--no-optional-locks`, and Codex's startup left the index unwritten too.

Numbers from https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/21328, measured in such a worktree:

| | fresh worktree | after one `git update-index -q --refresh` |
|---|---|---|
| Racily clean entries | 28,268 of 28,271 | 0 |
| `captureCheckpoint`, 5 in a row | 1,987–2,030 ms each | 209–266 ms each |
| T3 local status (`statusDetailsLocal`) | 3,734–3,774 ms each | 83–127 ms each |

On acerlinux, real T3 thread worktrees still had their creation-time index days later.

## Change

`GitVcsDriverCore.createWorktree` now refreshes the new worktree's index once, [...]

title: fix(server): subagent threads settle with their parent instead of sweeping on their own
author: mikeohuo

body:
Hidden subagent threads were swept independently, including redundant pull-request lookups, while empty children could remain unsettled indefinitely. title: fix(server): a remote update points the service unit at the runtime it committed
author: Marve10s
head: 3a20f33b763c53cb623f38a0a7d395f17475728f
body:
Remote updates left the service definition pointing at the runtime that originally installed it. After enough updates, pruning that obsolete runtime made the next systemd/launchd start fail. Fixes [#17490](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/17490).

After a durable commit, the launcher repoints only the program version in its existing definition and reloads systemd. It preserves quoting, arguments, and the launch agent environment. Reconciliation failures cannot undo activation; terminal-state recovery retries them, including when the file is correct but the manager still has an older loaded definition. Explicit local selections, including downgrades, remain selected. A unit reassigned to another T3 home is left intact. Live rollback also retries reconciliation.

Local installation and launcher writes coordinate across processes, preventing a stale snapshot from overwriting a newer selection. Protocol 4 prevents an old supervising launcher from accepting an update that needs these guarantees. Upgrade an existing installation once locally with `t3 update --yes` or `t3 service install`; a deferred restart does not upgrade the running launcher, and a crash or ordinary manager restart in that window can leave the service stopped until a local service restart. The new launcher accepts valid protocol-3 durable state written by the old CLI. Pending database recovery is preserved even when the service definition was removed, with a foreground recovery command in the error.

R [...]

threads.body:
**🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Run the service-unit repoint in a `finally` block.**

Keep `sendMessage` before `#repointServiceUnit`. The child waits for `committed` after it sends `prepared`, so moving the repoint first would change the handoff order. Use `finally` so the repoint runs after an IPC rejection while the rejection still reaches `#enqueue` and its fatal-error handling.

✅ Addressed in commits 66d773e to 8ca46de

**🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🟠 Major** | **🏗️ Heavy lift**

**Serialize service-unit updates.**

`BootService.install` checks state, then writes the unit without holding a lock. The default CLI path uses `start=true`, so it skips the later state recheck. If the CLI writes a newer unit after `#repointServiceUnit` reads it, the launcher can replace it with its older snapshot. Use a shared inter-process lock around both writers, or use an atomic compare-and-swap.

✅ Confirmed as addressed by @juliusmarminge

replies.body: Fixed in [ddb1472](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/commit/ddb14723e645d82d3d540a2cccc70e711afcb667): BootService.install and launcher unit reconciliation now share the inter-process selection lease, and both re-read durable selection before writing. The focused cross-process installer/launcher test exercises contention; the no-lock negative control fails. The 95-test focused suite and current- [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

**Reject lease owners from an earlier boot. A reused PID can block the lease permanently.**

The lock directory sits in the T3 home on persistent disk. It survives a reboot. A crash or power loss can leave a lease behind if it happens while a process holds it. The launcher holds the unit lease for up to 30 s during `daemon-reload`, so this window is real.

After a reboot, the stale owner's PID can belong to an unrelated live process. Boot services tend to get similar PIDs on every boot, so reuse is likely. In that case, `process.kill(pid, 0)` succeeds or returns `EPERM`, and the code treats the owner as alive. Every acquisition then waits 30 s and throws.

The consequence for the launcher: `#handlePrepared` and `#returnToPrevious` call `#selectState`, so a failure there is fatal. The service restarts, retries the pending trial, and fails again in a loop. `t3 service install` also fails, with the generic `BootServiceInstallError` message. The only fix is to delete the lock directory by hand.

Put a boot identifier in the owner name. Treat any owner from another boot as dead.

✅ Addressed in commit 3034465

author: AI091
head: 2e5853eea45042d74e957883129bc1e1f0a4cc63
body:
Claude wrappers such as a plain `~/.local/bin/claude` launcher could still offer `claude update`, even when the native-path classifier rejected them. The shared maintenance resolver fell back to that updater, leaving a button that could report success without updating the owning installation.

Claude now opts into manual fallback through the shared maintenance definition. After: 53/53 passed, including actual temporary-file native symlinks, forwarding wrappers, and an unowned OpenCode executable, package owners, simulated Windows contexts, and fallback for other providers with rejected native-path predicates.

- Review round 1 found that a generic pred [...]

** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Keep fixed version paths manual-only.**

If `binaryPath` points directly to `/custom/claude/versions/2.1.314`, this condition selects the native updater. Claude installs a new version and updates its managed launcher, but the configured version path stays fixed. T3 continues to run the old version. Require a launcher that the updater can move before offering the update action. ([code.claude.com](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.md))

---

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Check Homebrew ownership before accepting this path.**

A symlink at `/home/me/claude/versions/bin/claude` can point to a Homebrew keg. The native predicate matches the symlink, so the resolver selects `claude update` before checking the real path. This bypasses `brew upgrade` and may leave the Homebrew installation unchanged.

Exclude Homebrew-shaped real paths from Claude’s native branch, and add a regression fixture for this symlink.

title: fix(web): preview recordings stay decodable after a viewport resize
author: MansTomb
head: 610d36f98e2d8345155f9067bba88e2a268b8bc0
body:
Resizing the Preview viewport while a desktop recording is running produced an MP4 whose frames after the resize were corrupt. The recorder preferred `avc1`, and Chromium's `avc1` muxing writes the codec description once, so the updated SPS/PPS for the new dimensions never reach the file.

The recorder now prefers the `avc3` MP4 profiles (`avc3`, `avc3.640028`, `avc3.42e01e`), which carry parameter sets in-band, and never picks `avc1`. The WebM fallback and the bitrate calculation are unchanged. The fix covers both capture paths: the raw display stream and the compositor stream, whose canvas also follows the source dimensions.

Taken over from @MansTomb's [#10495](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10495) by the maintainer. Their PR identified the cause, the Chromium recommendation, and measured the fix on Electron 43 / Chromium 150 (resize exports decoded fully with `avc3` and failed with `avc1`). The takeover drops the recorder extraction into a separate module and the manual Electron+FFmpeg script, which only existed for that extraction and did not run in CI, and brings the branch up to date with the compositor on `main`.

## Human decision before merging

Several developer reports say Apple's AVFoundation (Safari, iOS, QuickTime) refuses H.264 tracks tagged `avc3` while playing the same stream tagged `avc1`. This change tags every recording `avc3`, not only resized ones, and recordings are uploaded as thread attachments that the mobile app plays through AVPlayer. Pl [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Preserve native frame dimensions across viewport changes.**

For a recording that starts at 960×540, a later 390×700 frame becomes approximately 301×540. The exported frame remains 960×540. This permanently reduces the portrait frame's resolution and does not preserve its native dimensions.

The linked issue explicitly requires native frame dimensions. Keeping the canvas fixed avoids encoded-size changes, but it does not satisfy that requirement. Preserve native dimensions, or obtain an explicit change to the requirement before shipping this approach.

title: fix(terminal): use a byte budget for Ghostty scrollback
author: zero-two-rafaeltab
head: b67ba3000ce5654b3678d0059eba4102e39b2b8e
body:
## Problem

Ghostty interprets the pinned ABI’s `max_scrollback` as bytes, although T3 named the 10,000 value as rows. Running the reporter’s 12,000-line command in an attached web terminal on current main retained only about 700 history rows at the reproduced width, silently discarding older output.

## Change

Use an explicit 10,000,000-byte budget for web/desktop and Android, matching the [pinned Ghostty application default](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/blob/9f62873bf195e4d8a762d768a1405a5f2f7b1697/src/config/Config.zig#L1388). Retention remains width- and content-dependent; this does not promise exactly 10,000 rows or change the ABI. A production-core/WASM regression checks retained history, and a committed numbered-output fixture reproduces the report in a real terminal.

Credit to [@zero-two-rafaeltab](https://github.com/zero-two-rafaeltab) for identifying the mismatch and contributing the fix.

Fixes https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/8701
